note.content: RESOLVED 2026-07-16. Fixed with two coupled thermodynamic corrections (no clamps): (1) conservative energy ddt using the CONTINUITY density rho_cont = rho_old - dt*div(phi) rebuilt from the final mass flux (new fvm::ddt_coeff_old), so (rho_cont-rho_old)/dt = -div(phi) exactly and the h*div(phi) term cancels term-for-term against div(phi h), restoring rho Dh/Dt = dp/dt -- this is approach (a) from the bead; (2) pressure-eqn compressibility psi = d(rho)/dp|_h (central finite-diff of the (p,h) flash at fixed enthalpy) replacing the frozen quality-weighted isothermal rho*kappa_T, which was ~100x too small in the two-phase dome and let the pressure overshoot through the plateau. Results: GS-1 flashing plateau 17 -> 393 psia (target ~350-367); RMSE vs Data 276 -> 60 psia; stable full 600 ms; no non-physical subcooling (void grows gradually, fluid holds near p_sat). All 915 lib tests still green. See collaboration/edwards_tampines_regen/debug_log.md and tests/edwards_blowdown.rs doc comment. note.content: FIXED 2026-07-16. Root cause: not a physics limit of HEM but a numerical stiffness in the rarefied emptying tail. As the pipe empties past t~0.18s a cell rarefies in a localized runaway (rho 127->23->vacuum over ~350 steps); the conservative-EEqn diagonal rho_cont*V/dt collapses to its 1e-4 floor, the solve becomes ill-conditioned, and one step tips he from 951 kJ/kg to -7.3e6 kJ/kg -> below the 273.15K (p,h) edge -> panic. Both continuity and momentum KNP dissipation independently trigger it, so it is the explicit deferred correction being over-driven in the rarefied tail, not a sign error. Fix: rarefied-tail density taper on the KNP blend beta *= clamp((rho_face-50)/(100-50),0,1), rho_face=min(rho_o,rho_nb). Dissipation zero below 50 kg/m3 (rarefied -> pure PIMPLE, stable), full above 100. Measured min dissipated-face density over the 0-0.15s ringing window is 106.5 kg/m3, so the taper is inert there. Results: full 600ms HybridAllMach completes (no panic/NaN, void in [0,1]), plateau 387.7 psia, GS-1 RMSE 30.6 psia, no cold tail; 0-0.15s ringing -55.5% and plateau retained bit-identically; default Pimple bit-identical (920 lib tests pass). See collaboration/edwards_tampines_regen/hybrid_stability_debug_log.md + figures_hybrid_stable/. Not committed (maintainer commits).

MAINTAINER'S CALL, 2026-08-06: not a blocker, and not to be treated stringently for artwork purposes.

The packing baked in crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/components/pebble_packing.rs is ARTWORK. Its structure is settled — solid fraction stable at 0.6069 / 0.6101 / 0.6112 across measurement windows, against ~0.61 for a real pebble bed — and that is the only property the drawing depends on. The residual creep (rms ~4% of a pebble radius, steady rather than decaying) does not affect how it looks.

So: DO NOT re-run, re-settle, post-process or otherwise chase equilibrium for the sake of the widgets. Use the bake as-is.

This bead stays open because the underlying limitation is REAL and would matter if the DEM is ever used for physics rather than pictures: simulation.rs's tangential contact is history-free (a Coulomb-capped dashpot with no accumulated tangential spring), so there is no static friction and a grain on an inclined contact creeps indefinitely. Strict rest is unreachable. That is worth fixing when someone wants granular DEM results, not before.

Dropped to reflect that it gates nothing currently in flight. The honest caveat in the module doc STAYS — documenting the limitation costs nothing and prevents the packing being cited later as a settled-equilibrium result. Documenting it is not the same as being stringent about it.

note.content:
MAINTAINER ARCHITECTURAL ANALYSIS + PROPOSED FALLBACK, 2026-08-13. Written up in full at
crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/docs/heat-exchanger-temperature-cross-fallback.md (DESIGN ONLY, not implemented).

THE DIAGNOSIS (maintainer's, and it is correct): 'across arrays, the coupling becomes explicit again. we should
expect temperature cross in that case.' The exchanger is THREE separate matrix systems -- hot array, tube metal,
cold array -- coupled through conductance terms at the previous iterate. Making convection implicit WITHIN an array
removes the intra-array Courant limit and does nothing for the inter-array coupling lag. So the 1-substep failure
is expected behaviour of an explicitly-coupled exchanger at a coarse coupling step, not a bug.

Measured with the helium side already implicit: 8 substeps -> ratio 1.027; 4 -> 2.051; 2 -> 4.101;
1 -> TEMPERATURE CROSS at physics/mod.rs:946, the second-law assertion, NOT a divergence of the helium array.

MONOLITHIC SOLVE REJECTED by the maintainer: 'a fully implicit solver would sort this out. albeit at a great cost as
I think it would wreck the entire matrix system. I don't really want that.' It would replace three cheap tridiagonal
solves with one large coupled system.

THE PROPOSED HEURISTIC -- adopt the steady-state temperature profile when a cross is observed, so thermodynamics is
not violated even though the transient differs:
  Tier 1: couple the two arrays DIRECTLY through an appropriate series thermal resistance, and set the metal to the
          temperature implied at that steady state rather than integrating it. (This is the Schur-complement
          elimination in concrete form -- the metal has no advection, so it is a per-node capacitance with two
          conductances and can be removed analytically, taking one full lag out of the coupling loop.)
  Tier 2: if a cross persists, compute steady-state outlet temperatures by LMTD and adjust both arrays' profiles to
          that LMTD-consistent profile.
  Invariant: the state handed to the next timestep must contain no temperature cross.

SIX CONCERNS RECORDED IN THE DOC, the first being the significant one:
  1. LMTD IS NOT VALID ACROSS A PHASE CHANGE, which is exactly where this exchanger lives. The cold side is
     feedwater -> steam through IF97; LMTD assumes constant cp, constant U and no phase transition. A single-zone
     LMTD across the boiling boundary will produce a confidently wrong profile. Standard fix is to ZONE the
     exchanger (subcooled / two-phase / superheat) with a per-zone U. Biggest technical risk in Tier 2.
  2. The fallback fires DURING transients -- precisely when the interesting dynamics are happening. Must be loud:
     counted, surfaced in the GUI, assertable in tests. Precedent: hot_enthalpy_clamp_events, currently zero
     everywhere and asserted == 0 in three tests.
  3. FIRST-LAW violation across the jump: overwriting both profiles changes stored energy discontinuously. Second
     law is respected pointwise; energy is not. Log the discrepancy per event and keep a running total.
  4. It can mask a genuine bug -- a cross at a substep count that should be fine is a bug signal, not a trigger.
  5. Chatter between fallback and transient integration; consider hysteresis or a minimum dwell.
  6. Cost must be measured. Tier 2 with zoning is not free and fires when the plant is already working hardest. If
     the fallback costs more than the substeps it saves, it is a net loss.

V&V FRAMING: results produced while the fallback is engaged are NOT a resolved transient and must never be presented
as one. Any validation claim against a measured transient is void for a run in which the fallback engaged.

NOT TRIED YET, on maintainer instruction ('don't try the correctors yet'): more INTER-ARRAY outer correctors. Worth
recording that the theory is favourable here in a way it is not for advection -- the inter-array Picard iteration's
contraction factor is roughly UA*dt/(m*cp), NOT the cell Courant number, so unlike the advective corrector loop it
can genuinely converge. Potentially cheaper than either tier.

note.content:
ALL THREE REMEDIES LANDED AND PUSHED 2026-08-13 (commit 3288145f on develop). Not wired in; default is None.

BEDOK ENTHALPY MARCH (Than Yan Ren, credited in the module doc with the singleflow1devap.m source and BEDOK snapshot):
  VERIFIED against a closed-form eps-NTU single-phase case -- hot outlet 0.135 K (0.086% of span), cold outlet
  0.011 K (0.033%), duty +0.086%. Boiling handled with NO zoning: 3 subcooled / 4 saturated / 1 superheated node
  simultaneously. Cost ~425 us per repair = 3.4% of one SG substep, which answers concern 6 of the design note --
  it fits the real-time budget comfortably. Two-point boundary problem solved by Illinois regula falsi bracketed
  between the two thermodynamic limits (never steps where the (p,h) flash has no answer), 5-9 iterations to
  1e-13..3e-7 K. Found and fixed a genuine defect: the hot capacity-rate inference divided by the drop to the last
  CELL CENTRE rather than the outlet FACE, a +5.97% bias walking the state 14.3 K hot / 38.7 K cold per engagement;
  after the closed-form correction the repair is a fixed point of itself to 7.8e-10.
  => ON THE MEASUREMENTS THIS IS THE BEST OF THE THREE. It is the only one with an analytic verification, the only
     one that handles phase change without zoning, and the cheapest.

ZONED LMTD: clears crosses (5.000 -> 0.000 K; 76.850 -> 0.000 K on 8 nodes), zones pinned at IF97 h_f/h_g with
  nothing fitted, bisection on duty with a monotone residual so convergence is unconditional. Settled LMTD vs
  eps-NTU by measurement: identical at C_r -> 0 (1.332e-12) and F = 1 to 1.278e-12.
  BUT THE COST IS LARGE: the imposed steady state is NOT the plant's operating point even at its own boundary
  conditions and calibrated UA -- 9.36 MW (-6.4%), steam outlet 366.2 degC vs published 440 (-73.8 K), helium
  return +30.9 K. Engaging it moves the plant by tens of kelvin. Most assumption-laden; try last.

ELIMINATE METAL: algebra verified three ways (5.684e-11 K vs numerically integrated ODE; both-sides equality to
  1 ulp; dropped axial conduction 1.704e-6 of the coupling). CANNOT CLEAR A CROSS and returns DidNotConverge every
  time BY CONSTRUCTION -- see the contract flaw below. Transient cost is the largest: tau_exchanger 39.78 s -> 0,
  tau_node 7.46 s -> 0, 31.78 MJ delivered early; 'not a different transient, a plant whose SG has no tube mass'.

CONTRACT FLAW -- MINE, and all three implementations hit it independently, which is conclusive:
  1. energy_discrepancy is not computable in joules. CrossRepairInputs carries mass FLOWS but no node masses,
     volumes or transit times, so no quantity with dimensions of joules is constructible. None of the three stubbed
     it; each states a rescalable inventory assumption instead.
  2. The cold profile is TEMPERATURES but the cold stream BOILS. Temperature does not determine state in two-phase
     and IF97 rejects the (T,p) flash at saturation outright, so latent content is unrecoverable. The contract must
     carry cold ENTHALPY. I documented exactly this reasoning on the cold_inlet_enthalpy field and then used
     temperatures for the profile anyway.
  3. No hot-fluid identity, so no hot-side EOS call is possible: LMTD assumes helium; Bedok INFERS C_hot from the
     supplied profiles and is thereby contaminated by the very state being repaired (a 40 K cross moves the inferred
     duty by 4.20%).
  4. EliminateMetal does not fit this contract at all -- it is an INTEGRATION-TIME change (swap four metal links for
     one direct hot-cold link at G_series), not a post-hoc state repair. Decide whether it belongs in this enum.

NEXT STEPS, in order: fix the contract (cold enthalpy profile, node inventory, timestep, metal heat capacity, hot
fluid identity); delete Bedok's C_hot inference once the fluid identity exists; then decide whether to wire dispatch
in at all. Note the shipped 2 substeps produce NO cross, so none of this is on the critical path -- it is the
answer to 'what if we ever need 1 substep', which would be worth roughly another 2x on top of the current 4.101x.

note.content:
ROOT-CAUSED 2026-08-21. The -3.03% elastic residual is NOT a defect in this port -- it is a property of the published ENDF/B-VIII.0 evaluation.

METHOD. Item 2 (full edge-by-edge comparison) done, and it answers item 1. Every SiC Bragg edge, published or regenerated, sits at E = n*E1 with n = h^2+k^2+l^2 on the conventional cell's simple-cubic reciprocal lattice (E1 = 1.066463 meV, the (100) spacing of a = 4.379 A), so n keys the two tables together independently of lattice constant, constants vintage and Debye-Waller treatment. Compared which reflections are extinguished.

RESULT (n <= 100, release, vs reference-data/endf/tsl-SiinSiC.endf):
  zinc-blende (what we ship):  35 reflections live in both, 25 EXTINCTION MISMATCHES
  'edge-centred' basis:        60 reflections live in both,  0 extinction mismatches

The tape carries a LIVE (100) reflection at 1.066463e-3 eV, plus live (210), (300)/(221), (320), (410)/(322), ... -- every mixed-parity reflection with ODD h+k+l, all of which zinc-blende extinguishes exactly. It extinguishes every mixed-parity reflection with EVEN h+k+l. That selection rule is the signature of the structure factor S = 1 + e^{i.pi.h} + e^{i.pi.k} + e^{i.pi.l}, whose |S|^2 is 16/4/0/4 for zero/one/two/three odd indices against fcc's 16/0/0/16. S is what you get from centring translations (1/2,0,0),(0,1/2,0),(0,0,1/2) -- 'half along each axis' -- instead of the fcc (0,1/2,1/2),(1/2,0,1/2),(1/2,1/2,0) -- 'half along each PAIR of axes'.

That basis is not a possible crystal: centring translations must be closed under addition mod the lattice for the atoms they generate to be symmetry-equivalent, and (1/2,0,0)+(0,1/2,0) = (1/2,1/2,0) is not a member. Pinned by its own test.

Feeding that basis through our own general path moves the thermal-point cross section 2.83347 -> 2.91289 b against the tape's 2.94078 b (all with the tape's own fitted 4W' = 5.977/eV) -- about 2.8 of the 3.0 percentage points.

REMAINING ~1%. Sits entirely in the weak |b_Si - b_C|^2 difference reflections (all-even hkl, h+k+l = 2 mod 4), running high +6.1% at n=20 rising monotonically to +23.5% at n=100. Growth with tau^2 confined to the difference reflections is the signature of a PER-ATOM-TYPE Debye-Waller factor in the evaluation (Zhu's 'exact' option) vs our single compound coefficient (Zhu's 'cubic approximation'). Separately the DW coefficients differ: 4W' = 5.977/eV (tape, 300 K) vs 5.382/eV (ours, 296 K), ~10% apart after temperature scaling -- not root-caused.

DECISION: we KEEP the physically correct zinc-blende structure and deliberately do NOT reproduce the tape. The 5% oracle band now brackets a known, characterised bias; tightening it would mean reproducing the evaluation's error.

ITEM 4 was already root-caused and the header was just stale: the general-vs-builtin divergence at 5 eV is NJOY's fixed index box (leapr.f90:2698,2725) not enclosing the tau^2 <= econ*Emax sphere, so the BUILT-IN path drops edges above ~0.8-1 eV. Asserted with measured ratios by general.rs::builtin_index_boxes_truncate_above_their_own_lattices_reach. Header corrected.

ITEM 3 done: both outram-mc-libs gap tests un-ignored and rewritten as live tolerance assertions.

ITEM 5 (Zhu & Hawari ICNC 2015 PDF) still not located -- left open, see follow-up bead.

ALL FINDINGS ARE AI-ASSISTED DRAFT. The central claim is about a published evaluation and needs human review before being cited or reported upstream.

note.content:
SOLVER CORE IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-12. crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/two_fluid.rs went from a 139-line scaffold whose step() returned NotYetImplemented to a working six-equation semi-implicit march (+2493 lines); two_fluid_tests.rs from a 12-line placeholder with zero tests to 18 verification tests (+1950 lines).

NOTE ON THIS BEAD'S TITLE: it says 'interfacial-pressure regularisation'. That is WRONG and was written before the source study. OpenFOAM's multiphaseEuler contains NO interfacial-pressure term at all -- no pInterface, no Stuhmiller, no Bestion, anywhere in the vendored tree (six-equation-regularisation.md section 1). What is implemented instead is VIRTUAL MASS folded inside the implicit 2x2 phase-coupling block, plus residualAlpha flooring, which is what upstream actually does for a fluid-fluid pair.

WHAT WAS BUILT:
- PhaseCouplingBlock / PhaseCouplingInputs: the 2x2 implicit drag + virtual-mass block per face, inverted in closed form. det = A_g A_l + A_g c_l + A_l c_g, a sum of non-negative terms, so it cannot lose its sign to cancellation and is strictly positive wherever residual-alpha flooring holds the diagonals up.
- Pressure equation derived from the VOLUME CONSTRAINT (sum of the phase continuity equations each divided by rho_k), so the flashing appears as a volumetric source Gamma (1/rho_g - 1/rho_l) and there is no kink to linearise across -- unlike drift flux, no secant is needed.
- Outer correctors are a proper Newton iteration on the volume residual R = alpha_g + alpha_l - 1, with the quasi-Jacobian -(V/dt) dR/dp assembled once per step. The first draft mixed a linearisation about p_old with a Newton correction and STALLED at R ~ 1e-4; fixed.
- Compressibilities taken along the ISENTROPIC path dh_k = dp/rho_k rather than at fixed enthalpy, because the energy equation applies the work term in the same step. Using the fixed-enthalpy derivative was measured to stall the correctors.
- Interfacial heat transfer solved IMPLICITLY in the phase enthalpies (closed form Q = dT/(1/K + dt/(m cp))), which is unconditionally stable and self-limiting.
- Conserved primary state is (m_g, m_l, m_g h_g, m_l h_l); alpha and rho are derived. Nothing is renormalised: the volume residual is reported and refused above 1e-4.

HONESTY: the regularisation is documented as TRACED TO UPSTREAM PRACTICE and explicitly NOT proven to restore hyperbolicity. No characteristic analysis was done, here or upstream, and two upstream tutorials run with no regularising term at all.

FOLLOW-UP BEADS FILED (7): the tampines-steam-tables Region-4 panic (P1); the low-void expansion-work refusal that BLOCKS a two-fluid Edwards case; the undiagnosed corrector non-convergence at small bubble diameter; the missing Dirichlet-pressure boundaries; the measured drift-flux/two-fluid compressibility disagreement; the virtual-mass port into outram-foam-multiphase; and performance.

note.content:
DONE and PUSHED 2026-08-13 (commit 3acc9536 on develop).

Real-time ratio 0.492 -> 1.032, independently re-verified: 20 s of plant time in 19.385 s wall, isolated release run.

KEY FINDING -- the global 0.1 s timestep was NOT the win. Sweep: 1 ms 0.492, 10 ms 0.505, 100 ms 0.514. The steam
generator runs on its own clock and is ~96% of the cost, so raising the plant step bought 4%. The 2x came from the
exchanger's PIMPLE outer correctors being set to 4 when settled duty is identical at 1, 2, 3 and 4 (9.6854 MW each
against a 9.6851 MW half-substep reference). Cost is exactly linear in correctors; two of four were paid for nothing.

The timestep work still earned its keep: unifying a dozen scattered literals into PLANT_TIMESTEP_S is what EXPOSED
both the wasted correctors and a -84.5% point-kinetics error at 0.1 s (Lambda/beta = 0.154 s is comparable to the
step; fixed by sub-stepping kinetics at 1 ms). It also caught a live bug where a test window had silently doubled to
150 s and was running to 999.07 K against a 1000 K limit.

Courant measured, not assumed: Co_hot 0.222 at 0.0125 s, 1.776 at 0.1 s, hot side binding at 4.97x the cold.
Correctors provably do not lift the limit -- 0.05 s panics at 4, 8 and 16; 0.1 s at 8 and 32.

Clamp events zero everywhere, now asserted == 0 in three tests.

Accuracy: reactor power +0.0000% (STRUCTURAL -- both runs integrate kinetics at 1 ms, not a convergence result),
core outlet -0.0015 K, bed -0.054 K, SG duty -0.012%. WORSE: steam outlet +0.822 K, GUI 100 Hz -> 10 Hz.

Follow-on: op-3lay (build real buffer -- 1.032 is ~3% margin and goes negative under load).

note.content: Root-cause analysis (2026-07-24, from the op-6tz.34 work). The reflective-corner stuck-history is grazing-incidence ping-pong: a particle moving nearly parallel to a reflective wall, near a corner, alternately hits the two/three perpendicular walls at sub-nudge distances. Each fixed 1e-9 cm nudge advances it only ~1e-9 cm ALONG the wall, so traversing an O(1 cm) feature needs ~1e9 bounces >> MAX_EVENTS=100k -> the history is capped and leaked (the band-aid). This is distinct from op-6tz.34 (now fixed): that was a lattice-edge/wall coincident tie leaking histories OUT of the box; this is in-corner non-progress. A PROPER fix (per this bead: do NOT extend the band-aid) needs OpenMC-style token-based surface tracking (advance exactly to the surface, resolve the next cell by surface index + sense, and compose a corner reflection off all coincident reflective surfaces in one event) rather than a fixed position nudge. That is a larger rework best done against the OpenMC reference source (not available in this sandbox), so leaving open with this analysis. The residual ~2% surface-vs-delta gap in the op-6tz.34 regression test is plausibly this effect.

note.content: Fixed in 69d8874 (integrated onto claude/outram-mc-setup-cb1bg9, which has op-6tz.34). Root cause: cross_surface reflective arm reflected a grazing near-corner particle off only the primary wall; the fixed 1e-9 cm nudge left it headed into the perpendicular wall(s), re-crossing at sub-nudge distances (~1e5-1e9 events → MAX_EVENTS leak, negative bias). Fix: Geometry::compose_corner_reflection composes the specular reflection of every reflective/white/periodic surface coincident with the crossing point (|evaluate(r)|<=1e-9) that the particle actually crosses (|u·n|>0, sign-agnostic for min/max-side axis-aligned walls). Retroreflection at a right-angle corner → particle leaves in one event. Lone-wall case is bit-identical to surf.reflect. MAX_EVENTS/NUDGE untouched. Tests: corner_reflection_composes_at_exact_corner (unit), corner_grazing_history_terminates_without_pingpong (worst 100003→4 events, 20→0 leaks), corner_reflective_cube_surface_tracking_unbiased (surface 2.22235±0.00334 vs delta 2.21925±0.00320, 0.67σ). 158 lib + 30 notebook tests pass; op-6tz.34 nested-lattice test still green. THE BEAD'S PREMISE CHANGED. It was filed saying the wiring 'needs thermal-scattering data not present on this host' and depended on the download path (op-6tz.28). The data-availability half no longer holds: all 33 ENDF/B-VIII.0 LEAPR decks are embedded in njoy-outram-park-fork as of 2026-08-14, so every law regenerates offline with no download and no host-specific path. op-6tz.28 is NOT a blocker for this any more.

DESIGN FINDING -- this was never a triso_particle.rs change. That module assigns opaque material INDICES by design and its own doc says so. A thermal law binds to a Nuclide, not a material index, via Nuclide::with_thermal_scattering. So the wiring is caller-side composition; putting deck loading inside a CSG module would break the crate's data/transport boundary (outram-mc parses no ENDF). Representation: cyclic pairing stored as BoundaryPatch::cyclic_partner (partner patch index, half0/half1 same-local-index correspondence) + FvMesh::cyclic_couplings (Vec<CyclicCoupling> of owner<->neighbour cell couplings), derived at build time; FvMesh::periodic_1d builds a 1-D periodic ring programmatically. FINDING, and it is the one that matters for whoever wires the SiC layer: MAT 43 and MAT 44 carry BYTE-IDENTICAL MF=7/MT=2 sections -- 1044 records each, differing only in the header line's ZA/AWR (verified by extracting MT=2 from both tapes and diffing columns 1-66; 1043 of 1044 lines match exactly). Not a parser bug and not an evaluator error: coherent elastic scattering is a property of the 3C-SiC lattice as a whole, not of one sublattice, so one structure factor is delivered in both materials.

Consequence: a transport code that builds a SiC region from both S(alpha,beta) materials and sums their elastic channels DOUBLE-COUNTS the Bragg scattering. MT=2 must be attributed to the compound once -- assigned to one sublattice or split -- not carried by both nuclides. Written up in reference-data/endf/README.md.

Closing: the tape is here. The double-counting question belongs to op-t33q / op-6tz.35 where the layer actually gets wired.

note.content:
ROOT CAUSE ESTABLISHED AND EXACTLY REPRODUCED, 2026-08-06. Three independent investigations converged.

MECHANISM (certain):
surface_distance.wgsl:298   let c0 = gc * gc - 4.0 * a2 * gamma;

For the failing ray the two operands are BIT-IDENTICAL f32 values (both 6.7599992752075195), i.e. 100% cancellation, all 24 mantissa bits lost. The true value is exactly 0 -- confirmed in exact rational arithmetic: gc^2 - 4*a2*gamma = 2.6^2 - 4*1.69 = 6.76 - 6.76 = 0.

- Rust does NOT contract mul+sub, so the CPU f32 mirror computes c0 = 0.0 exactly. The degenerate root stays at exactly 0 (measured -1.78e-15) and the t <= eps filter discards it. Correct answer 0.49672258 returned.
- The GPU backend IS permitted to fuse gc*gc - X into an FMA (one rounding instead of two), which keeps gc^2 exact and yields c0 = +2.2888184503244702e-07 -- about half an ULP of 6.76, a value not even representable as a difference of two f32 near 6.76.
- That perturbs the root at 0 to t = -c0/c1 = 3.1208810e-07. Running the full WGSL algorithm in float32 both ways:
    no FMA: c0=0           roots=[-1.78e-15, 0.49672258]  -> 4.967226e-01
    FMA:    c0=2.2888e-7   roots=[3.120881e-07, 0.49672228] -> 3.120881e-07
  EXACT match to the reported GPU value 3.120881e-7 (8 significant figures).

WHY THE ORIGIN MATTERS: the test origin (0,-1.3,0) lies EXACTLY on the torus outer equator (a+b = 1.0+0.3 = 1.3), so the quartic has an exact root at t=0 and c0 is exactly 0. The fixture passes coincident:false for a point that IS coincident.

THREE CONDITIONS, ALL TRUE:
1. Total cancellation makes c0 pure rounding noise whenever the origin is on the surface.
2. FMA contraction is legal AND UNCONTROLLABLE: grep -rn NoContraction over naga-29.0.3/29.0.4 returns NOTHING -- naga never emits the SPIR-V NoContraction decoration, so the driver is free to fuse. This is the entire CPU/GPU divergence; the algorithm is otherwise identical.
3. The filter at wgsl:302 is an ABSOLUTE eps = 1.0e-7, roughly 10x BELOW the measured f32 noise floor for this geometry: ulp(gc^2)/|c1| = 8e-7/0.733 = 1.1e-6. The f64 reference (geometry/surface.rs:880) uses 1e-10/1e-8; the f32 twin scaled eps by only 1000x while the noise floor grew by ~1e9x. Any c0 perturbation of half an ULP or more yields a root >= 1.6e-7, which ALWAYS passes.

Neither existing filter catches it: the spurious-branch test G(t) = +2.6 > 0 PASSES, so the fake root sits on the geometrically correct branch. The root-finder is NOT at fault -- it correctly returns a genuine root of the quartic it was handed.

EMPIRICAL SCOPE (independent agent, full 19440-query sweep on the real adapter):
- 79 mismatches / 19440 = 0.41%
- Non-torus surfaces 0-11: ZERO mismatches across 15552 queries. Completely clean.
- XTorus 70, ZTorus 9, YTorus 0.
- ALL 79 come from the 5 (surface, origin) pairs where the origin lies exactly on the torus (implicit residual 2.2e-16). Perfect correlation, no false positives or negatives.
- The GPU is NEVER larger and NEVER misses when the CPU hits. Every mismatch is a spurious tiny root: min 1.006e-7 (barely over the 1e-7 threshold), median 1.85e-7, max 3.5e-6.
- YTorus is clean ONLY because none of the 27 lattice origins happens to sit on it -- predicted from the mechanism alone: on-surface origin counts are XTorus 4/27, ZTorus 1/27, YTorus 0/27, exactly matching the observed failure pattern.
- The trusted f64 path agrees with the CPU f32 mirror in every case sampled (q16033: f64 = 4.96722659144033e-1, cpu_f32 = 4.9672258e-1, gpu = 3.12e-7). THE CPU IS THE CORRECT SIDE.

FIX CONSTRAINTS (things that will NOT work, established):
- Normalising the quartic changes nothing: c4 = ga^2 = 1.0 exactly here, the quartic is already monic, and all coefficients are O(1). Nothing overflows or underflows f32.
- Disabling FMA is not available: naga emits no NoContraction decoration.
- Reformulating c0 as a difference of squares (gc-2a*sqrt(gamma))(gc+2a*sqrt(gamma)) only halves the error -- gc and 2a*sqrt(gamma) are themselves 2.6 vs 2.6, still cancelling. Not a real fix.

FIX MUST ADDRESS THE NOISE FLOOR. Candidates:
(a) Snap c0 to exactly 0 when |c0| is at or below the rounding noise of the cancelled subtraction, e.g. |c0| <= K * ulp(gc*gc). Directly cancels the FMA artifact and restores CPU/GPU agreement at the source.
(b) Make eps RELATIVE to the conditioning: eps = max(current, K * ulp(max|coeff|)/|c1|), i.e. track the ~1.1e-6 noise floor rather than a fixed 1e-7.
(c) Both. Apply the same change to the Rust f32 mirror so the twin stays a twin.

NOTE this is only partly a fixture artifact. A real transport run has particles sitting on and just off surfaces constantly, so the on-surface case is the norm, not a corner. Also: with coincident:true the eps becomes 1e-5, which WOULD filter 3.12e-7 -- so a caller that correctly flags coincidence escapes the bug.
note.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop

note.content:
FIXED 2026-08-06. Verified on NVIDIA RTX A5000 / NVK GA102 / Vulkan.

TWO CHANGES, applied IDENTICALLY to both sides (shaders/surface_distance.wgsl and the Rust f32 mirror in gpu/surface_distance.rs), because the whole defect was the two drifting apart:

1. SNAP c0 TO ZERO BELOW ITS OWN ROUNDING NOISE.
   c0_raw = gc*gc - 4*a2*gamma
   c0_noise = C0_CANCELLATION_ULPS * F32_EPS * max(|gc*gc|, |4*a2*gamma|)
   c0 = 0 when |c0_raw| <= c0_noise
   Below that threshold the value carries no information -- it is indistinguishable from zero in f32 -- so this removes the FMA-vs-two-rounding divergence at source rather than downstream.

2. MAKE THE ROOT GATE TRACK THE NOISE FLOOR instead of sitting under it.
   eps = max(base_eps, min(c0_noise / |c1|, EPS_CAP))
   A residual perturbation dc0 displaces a simple root near zero by dc0/|c1|. The old fixed 1.0e-7 sat roughly an order of magnitude BELOW the measured f32 noise floor (~1.1e-6) for cm-scale torus geometry, so noise roots always passed. EPS_CAP = 1.0e-3 cm (10 um) stops a near-zero c1 from widening the gate enough to swallow a real crossing.

New shared constants, spelled identically on both sides (WGSL has no f32::EPSILON): F32_EPS = 1.1920929e-7, C0_CANCELLATION_ULPS = 4.0, EPS_CAP = 1.0e-3.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES (all established during investigation, recorded so they are not retried):
- Normalising the quartic: c4 = ga^2 = 1.0 exactly here, it is already monic and all coefficients are O(1). Would change nothing.
- Disabling FMA: naga emits no NoContraction decoration anywhere, so contraction is not controllable from the shader.
- Reformulating c0 as a difference of squares (gc - 2a*sqrt(gamma))(gc + 2a*sqrt(gamma)): gc and 2a*sqrt(gamma) are themselves 2.6 vs 2.6, so it still cancels. Halves the error at best.

RESULT: gpu::surface_distance::tests::gpu_matches_cpu_reference PASSES over all 19440 queries and all 15 surface types. Previously 79 mismatches (XTorus 70, ZTorus 9, YTorus 0, non-torus 0 of 15552). Full crate suite: 197 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored. cargo check --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android clean.

NO TOLERANCE WAS LOOSENED -- the test's pass criterion is unchanged at |gpu-cpu| <= 1e-3*(1+|cpu|). The kernel now produces the right answer.

note.content:
FIXED 2026-08-06, in the same pass as op-9s8.11 (same two files, same class of defect: WGSL and the Rust mirror drifting apart).

Both sides now clamp the cubic's root count to the mathematical maximum:
  const MAX_CUBIC_REAL_ROOTS = 3
  WGSL cubic_real_roots: out.n = min(out.n, MAX_CUBIC_REAL_ROOTS) before returning
  Rust cubic_real_roots_f32: .min(MAX_CUBIC_REAL_ROOTS) on the returned count

That is what keeps quartic_real_roots' 3-element crits array and collect_real_roots' 5-element bp array in bounds: with ncr <= 3, nb reaches at most 1 + 3 + 1 = 5, so bp[5] is never written and crits[3] is never read.

On the Rust side the caller's 3-slot buffer already bounded the count, so the clamp is normally a no-op there -- it is stated explicitly so the invariant is enforced the same way on both sides, rather than resting on a buffer size on one side and nothing at all on the other. That asymmetry was the bug.

Verified: full crate suite 197 passed, 0 failed; cargo check --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android clean.

NOT directly regression-tested: the trigger needs a cubic whose clustered triple root splits by more than push_unique's dedup radius (the reproducer found by random search was cubic_real_roots(1.0, -2.30112, 1.19506, -0.179715) -> n = 4). A targeted unit test for that input would be worth adding; filing that thought here rather than claiming coverage we do not have.

MAINTAINER DECISION 2026-08-11: the metadata-only approach for huang2025waterIngress is APPROVED. Maintainer: 'I think you made the right decision on huang2025.'

So the standing rule for a document whose copyright line reserves text and data mining / AI training rights: catalogue the bibliographic metadata and the factual findings, and DO NOT run bulk full-text extraction into the corpus. The paper stays fully usable — read it, cite it, implement correlations from it, record its numbers with provenance, because facts are not copyrightable. Only the machine-readable full-text corpus is withheld.

Currently affected: huang2025waterIngress ALONE. A grep audit of all seven proprietary PDFs on 2026-08-11 found the clause in no other document; the earlier full-text ingests (wu2002, gao2002, wang2014, tantillo2020, xhonneux2014, tobias1980) carry no such reservation and need no action.

REMAINING WORK on this bead: make the rule enforceable rather than remembered. A future ingest should DETECT the reservation clause and refuse or warn, instead of relying on whoever is ingesting to read the copyright page carefully. Grep terms that caught it: 'text and data mining', 'AI training'. That check belongs next to the visibility inference in the ingestion path.

The limit was self-imposed, not hardware. src/gpu/mod.rs probe() requested wgpu::Limits::downlevel_defaults(), which pins max_storage_buffers_per_shader_stage to 4. surf_dist.bgl binds 7 storage buffers (bindings 0-5 and 7; binding 6 is a uniform), so create_bind_group_layout rejected it.

note.content:
CORRECTION TO COMMIT e11989a7's MESSAGE, recorded 2026-08-11.

That commit says 'test 24 bare-HEM: mean|dev| = 9.0%' and frames it as 'HEM tracks the full-scale Marviken data to about 9% on average'. **That framing is misleading and this note is the correction of record**, since the commit is already pushed and cannot be cleanly amended.

THE ACTUAL RESULT, from the fleet's final report:
- Test 23 (3 K subcooling): VALIDATED. Mean |dev| 12.6%, inside a measured +/-25%-per-point digitisation budget.
- Test 24 (33 K subcooling): **NOT validated through the production dispatcher — a -48.5% SYSTEMATIC deficit.**
- The 9.0% (test 24) and 10.1% (test 23) figures are from the **bare HEM maximum-flux criterion**, NOT the production path.

So the commit quoted a bare-criterion number as if it characterised the model's production behaviour, and omitted that the dispatcher is nearly 50% low on test 24.

WHY THAT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS GOOD NEWS: the gap between the bare criterion (9.0%) and the dispatcher (-48.5%) is the evidence that this is a SOLVER BRANCH-SELECTION DEFECT, not a limitation of HEM physics. HEM itself reproduces test 24 to 9%; the dispatcher is picking the wrong branch. That is this bead, it is P1, and it is fixable — unlike a physics limitation, which would not be.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE CROSS-FIDELITY COMPARISON: the sibling fleet building drift-flux and two-fluid Marviken cases was released against a stated HEM reference. They must compare against the BARE-CRITERION numbers (9.0% / 10.1%) as the honest HEM baseline, NOT the dispatcher's -48.5%, which reflects this defect rather than the equilibrium assumption. Comparing a higher-fidelity model against a broken branch selection would flatter it for the wrong reason.

Also corrected in the same report: test 23's subcooling is 3 K, not 33 K, against NUREG/CR-2671.

Location: get_critical_pressure_and_mass_flux_subcooled_liquid_ph, in
crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/steam_turbine_equations/converging_diverging_nozzles/choked_flow/stagnation_point_outside_vle_ph_dome_multiphase.rs,
inserted immediately after `subcooling_ratio` is computed and before the `if subcooling_ratio > DEEP_SUBCOOLING_RATIO` branch. It required hoisting `let x_at_energy = two_phase_quality(p_energy, s0);` above that branch (it currently lives below it).

What it printed, one eprintln! per call, prefixed PROBE:
  branch       — which of the three arms is taken: "deep_escape" (subcooling_ratio > DEEP_SUBCOOLING_RATIO), "sonic_kink" (x_at_energy < 0.03), or "energy"
  p0_MPa, h0_kJkg, T0_K   — the stagnation state
  dTsub_K      — sat_temp_4(p0) - T0, i.e. actual stagnation subcooling (NaN above p_crit)
  subratio     — the subcooling_ratio the deep-escape test uses
  x_at_energy  — the quality at the energy-maximum choke, i.e. the sonic-kink discriminator
  p_bub_MPa, p_energy_MPa, pe_over_pb   — the two candidate choke pressures and their ratio
  g_energy, g_sonic, ratio_ge_gs        — the two candidate mass fluxes and their ratio
  interior     — g_two_phase >= g_bubble, i.e. whether the energy max is a genuine interior stationary point or just the bubble endpoint
  g_two_phase, g_bubble

Purpose: the bead's thesis is that the Marviken test-24 points land in the "overlap zone" where subcooling_ratio never reaches DEEP_SUBCOOLING_RATIO = 5.0 while x_at_energy < 0.03, so the solver takes the bubble-point sonic-kink branch (rho_f * c_2phi) when it should not. The probe is what turns that from an inference into per-point evidence: run the Marviken gate with it in place and read the branch / subratio / x_at_energy columns for the 40 test-24 points.

1-D SIX-EQUATION SOLVER IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-12 under op-62vf. crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/two_fluid.rs is no longer a scaffold: step() marches.

DoD status against this bead's 'theory + verification + benchmark + unit-safe uom':
  theory      DONE. Module docs carry the full six-equation set, the derivation of the pressure equation from the volume constraint, and the regularisation with its provenance.
  verification DONE. 18 tests in two_fluid_tests.rs: the 2x2 block algebra against closed forms, both vanishing-phase limits (exact to 1e-15 at alpha = 0), the no-slip limit (1/K_d asymptote to 3 figures), exact mass conservation, a well-balanced check that returns identical zeros, the interfacial energy identity to 4.15e-11, monotone thermal relaxation over five decades, and a regression for a phase-extinction bug.
  benchmark   NOT DONE, and BLOCKED -- see the low-void bead. Edwards-O'Brien starts 57 K subcooled, which is exactly the regime the solver refuses.
  unit-safe uom DONE at the API boundary; the marching loop is raw f64 in strict SI with every boundary documented, matching drift_flux.

TRACE-BACK CONSTRAINT HONOURED, with one stated exception. Drag comes from outram_foam_multiphase::two_fluid::DragModel and heat transfer from outram_foam_multiphase::heat_transfer::InterfacialHeatTransfer, both through super::interfacial rather than reimplemented. The exception is VIRTUAL MASS: InterfacialForce::VirtualMass upstream is an unported scaffold returning NotImplemented, so the formula is transcribed locally from OpenFOAM dispersedVirtualMassModel.C:51-67 via the source study, with the deviation stated in its doc comment and a bead filed to port it properly.

ALSO CORRECTED: two_fluid.rs used to claim the 3-D reference 'has no interfacial heat-transfer closure at all -- it is isothermal -- so there is nothing to trace back to'. That became false when outram_foam_multiphase::heat_transfer was ported; the module docs now say so explicitly rather than leaving a doc that misdescribes the codebase.

note.content:
SEQUENCING (maintainer, 2026-08-04): 'the 1D versions of drift flux and 6 eqn are to be the bread and butter of tampines before the AI is in... Before PINNs and other AI accelerations of the solver are in.'

So the 1D REDUCED models are the primary deliverable, not the full 3D CFD ports. Those already have beads: op-dt3.12 (1D Drift Flux), op-dt3.13 (1D Two-Fluid), op-dt3.14 (1D CHF), op-dt3.15 (1D Dryout), op-dt3.16 (1D Post-Dryout). This bead is the umbrella that says where the physics comes FROM (outram-foam-multiphase) and that it sits above the HEM baseline (op-dt3.18).

Order: HEM baseline (op-dt3.18) -> 1D drift-flux + 1D 6-eqn (op-dt3.12/.13) as the workhorse solvers -> only THEN PINNs / AI acceleration. The 'AI' in the TAMPINES acronym is explicitly a LATER stage; the deterministic 1D solvers must be the trustworthy baseline it is measured against first.

ClaRa licence verified directly 2026-08-04 (not from a search summary):

BSD-3-Clause confirmed at THREE levels, all agreeing:
1. Repo LICENSE at xrg-simulation/ClaRa-official — verbatim standard BSD 3-Clause text. Copyright 2013-2023, ClaRa development team = TLK-Thermo GmbH (Braunschweig) + XRG Simulation GmbH (Hamburg).
2. Per-file header on ClaRa/Components/TurboMachines/Turbines/SteamTurbineVLE_L1.mo (v1.9.0): 'Licensed by the ClaRa development team under the 3-clause BSD License. Copyright 2013-2024.' Identical in the ClaRaLibrary/ClaRa mirror.

Original contribution: DYNCAP/DYNSTART development team, 2011-2024, funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (FKZ 03ET2009, FKZ 03ET7060).

FOUR CAVEATS:
- GitHub's licence detector reports NOASSERTION / 'Other' for the repo. FALSE ALARM — caused by the malformed copyright line 'Copyright (c) Copyright 2013-2023,' defeating the strict matcher. Licence body is unmodified BSD-3. Expect automated scans to flag it.
- Use xrg-simulation/ClaRa-official, NOT ClaRaLibrary/ClaRa: the latter has NO LICENSE file at repo root (GitHub API 404), only per-file headers.
- Every ClaRa file warns 'Contents published in ClaRa have been contributed by different authors and institutions. Please see model documentation for detailed information on original authorship and copyrights.' Per-model provenance CAN differ from the blanket licence. SteamTurbineVLE_L1.mo was checked and is clean — do NOT generalise that to other ClaRa models without checking each one.

Dependency: the turbine model imports TILMedia functions. The TILMediaClaRa submodule (TLK-Thermo/TILMediaClaRa) is itself BSD-3-Clause, cleanly detected. We do not need it anyway — our property layer is IF97 via TampinesSteamTableCV, so a port takes the Stodola/efficiency/rotor algebra and drops the media calls.

Bonus finding: SteamTurbineVLE_L1.mo already has useMechanicalPort, steadyStateTorque, rpm_fixed and moment of inertia J — i.e. it implements the rotor-inertia coupling this scope calls for in op-dt3.23. Independent confirmation of the design direction.

note.content:
LIKELY RESOLVED BY op-fm5's fix (2026-08-11) -- maintainer to confirm and close.

The mechanism this bead describes no longer exists. As of chem-eng 0.2.0, TransferFnFirstOrder does not accumulate a FirstOrderResponse per input change: both of its constituent blocks (FirstOrderStableTransferFnNoZeroes and FirstOrderStableTransferFnForZeroes) now advance by an exact O(1) zero-order-hold recurrence carrying 2 and 1 state variables respectively, with no Vec and no 20*tau pruning. So nordheim_fuchs::advance_with_reactivity_driver can be driven in an always-on real-time loop at any timestep without the O(n)/step growth or unbounded memory.

Measured: filtered PID at dt=0.001 s with tau_d=80.8 s -- exactly the PRKE shape this bead worried about -- went from 2329.52 us/step and still rising at step 79,000, to a flat 0.17 us/step. Guarded by block_state_size_does_not_grow_with_step_index and pid_step_cost_does_not_grow_with_step_index in chem-eng.

No change was needed in teh-o-prke itself. Neither of the two remedies this bead proposed (an O(1) reactivity-lag path, or periodic rebasing) is required any more.

note.content:
FIXED 2026-08-21, commit 5a91ecf7, per the maintainer's explicit design
(GH #27 comment): a CachePolicy enum, not an automatic key fix.

CachePolicy::{AlwaysRegenerate, UseCacheIfAvailable} on SabRequest.cache,
set via with_cache(). AlwaysRegenerate is the default -- every request
computes fresh and never touches the on-disk cache at all (no read, no
write). UseCacheIfAvailable reuses a hit (log::warn! naming the staleness
risk and pointing at #27 on every hit), and falls back to generating fresh
-- never an error -- on a miss, populating the cache for next time.

Also bumped GENERATOR_REVISION 2 -> 3: the temperature-block-selection fix
(1a904fc5) changed output for HInH2O/DInD2O/OInD2O and should have bumped
it then but didn't. Documented as the concrete case study in the
constant's own doc comment, since GENERATOR_REVISION still exists and
still matters for UseCacheIfAvailable users -- the new policy doesn't
replace it, it makes the risk that mechanism can't fully close an explicit
opt-in instead.

Two new tests prove the actual bug scenario: one plants a deliberately
invalid tape under the real cache key and confirms AlwaysRegenerate never
reads it; the other confirms UseCacheIfAvailable falls back gracefully on
a miss and populates the cache.

Full njoy suite green (0 failures, 24 targets); workspace check clean;
clippy clean on the change.

Windows has no daemon (query() returns None, falls back to spawn-per-call) -- explicit, not silently degraded, per this bead's own original design note. Verified live: cold call ~35-54s (real rust-analyzer index), warm calls 0.1-1s, explicit stop confirmed (process exits, socket removed), stale-socket recovery exercised accidentally (a killed daemon's leftover socket file was correctly detected and replaced). Also found+fixed a real bug during testing: the daemon's original idle-timeout clock started at connection-ACCEPT not connection-FINISH, so a single slow first request (waiting out indexing) could make the daemon look 'idle' the instant it replied -- moot now that idle-timeout was removed entirely, but the fix is preserved in the commit history as a lesson (measure idle from when a request finishes, not when it starts, in any future daemon).

note.content:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-11 (awaiting maintainer review; NOT closed by the agent).

APPROACH CHOSEN: option 1, the exact O(1) recurrence. Not time-bucketing. The recurrence reproduces the pre-existing semantics EXACTLY rather than approximating them, so bucketing was not implemented and no grouping error had to be quantified. It is the zero-order-hold / step-invariant discrete equivalent, exact for piecewise-constant input; module docs cite Astrom & Wittenmark, Seborg et al., Franklin/Powell/Workman, Ogata, Hochbruck & Ostermann, Oppenheim & Schafer, and Smith (open access). No editions/years/pages given -- none verified against a physical copy.

SCOPE: all FIVE vector-carrying block types, in BOTH tiers (alpha_nightly and beta_testing), not just the first-order one named in the original report:
  first_order_transfer_fn.rs                (1 vec -> 2 scalars)
  first_order_transfer_fn_with_zeroes.rs    (2 vecs -> 1 scalar)
  second_order_transfer_fn.rs               (1 vec -> 3 scalars, enum per damping regime)
  decaying_sinusoid.rs                      (1 vec -> 2 scalars, decaying rotation)
  decaying_exponentials.rs                  (1 vec -> 3 scalars; alpha_nightly only)
The two tiers are now byte-identical apart from the tier import path; previously they had drifted (beta_testing's decaying_sinusoid had a '>' vs '>=' heaviside that dropped the cosine value at t == start_time; unified on alpha's correct '>=').

MEASURED, same harness before and after (release, AMD Ryzen 5 5600, rustc 1.97.0, 200-step windows, two 5,000-step warm-ups discarded). Baseline reproduces this bead's original figures:
  A PID dt=0.04, 40k:   28.35 us/step plateau -> 0.17 us/step;  1.188 s -> 0.007 s
  B PID dt=0.10, 40k:   13.15 us/step         -> 0.17 us/step;  0.478 s -> 0.007 s
  C PID dt=0.001, 80k: 1176.11 us/step plateau -> 0.17 us/step; 83.280 s -> 0.015 s   (the decisive case)
  D P only dt=0.04:      9.42 us/step         -> 0.06 us/step;  0.379 s -> 0.002 s
  E PID tau_d=1000 dt=0.04: 736.86 us/step still rising -> 0.17 us/step; 15.167 s -> 0.007 s
  F PID tau_d=80.8 dt=0.001 (the PRKE shape): 2329.52 us/step still rising -> 0.17 us/step; 127.599 s -> 0.014 s
Per-step cost is now FLAT in the step index in every case, including E and F whose retirement horizons are never reached.

PHYSICS UNCHANGED: the summed output over each of the six runs is identical before and after to the three decimal places printed (e.g. case A sink 17175484.304 both times). The only intended difference is that the old code discarded exp(-20) = 2.06e-9 of each step response when it retired one; the recurrence carries that residual, so the new answer is marginally MORE accurate.

VERIFICATION (methodology + results in each test doc comment): each recurrence checked against the closed-form analytic superposition of the retained response structs, over 2000 steps, tolerance 1e-9. Max abs differences measured 2026-08-11: first order 6.33e-15; with zeroes 1.69e-15; second order 9.05e-15 / 5.11e-15 / 6.94e-15 (zeta = 0.35 / 1.0 / 2.4); decaying sinusoid 4.16e-16 sine, 4.86e-16 cosine; decaying exponential 8.60e-16 overdamped, 6.66e-16 critically damped; irregular time grid 7.99e-15; dead time 6.11e-15. All round-off, not discretisation error.

REGRESSION TESTS (would have caught the original defect):
  block_state_size_does_not_grow_with_step_index -- 100k steps at dt=0.001 with tau=80.8 s; state size identical at step 100 and step 99,999 ([2,1,3,2,3] alpha, [2,1,3,2] beta). Pre-0.2.0 the counts would have been 101 and 100,000.
  pid_step_cost_does_not_grow_with_step_index (alpha) -- filtered PID tau_d=80.8 s at dt=0.001: 0.172 us/step @5k -> 0.175 us/step @100k, ratio 1.02; bare P 0.059 -> 0.060, ratio 1.02.
  first_order_step_cost_does_not_grow_with_step_index (beta) -- 0.0550 -> 0.0570 us/step, ratio 1.04.

CAPABILITIES PRESERVED: irregular/arbitrary timesteps (the recurrence uses the actual elapsed time per call, verified by a dedicated test) and dead time (queued in a VecDeque bounded by delay/dt -- 26 entries for 0.25 s of dead time at dt=0.01, flat over a 2000-step run; empty when there is no dead time). New precondition, documented: simulation time must be non-decreasing.

FLAKY TEST FOUND AND FIXED (uncommitted, in tree). The two wall-clock step-cost regression tests I added asserted a late-vs-early ratio below 5x from a SINGLE timed 2,000-step window per checkpoint. note.content:
ITEM 1 DONE 2026-08-21, commit 26395482. Per-atom-type Debye-Waller (Zhu's 'exact' option) implemented and measured; the shape argument that predicted it is confirmed.

MEASURED. Residual against the published tape, per difference reflection (all-even hkl, h+k+l = 2 mod 4):
  n     compound      per-atom
  4      +2.8 %        +2.0 %
  12     +4.8 %        +2.0 %
  20     +6.9 %        +1.9 %
  36    +11.1 %        +1.9 %
  44    +13.4 %        +1.9 %
  52    +15.7 %        +1.9 %
Compound residual grows 5.6x across the range; per-atom is FLAT to within 0.1 percentage point. The tau-dependent component is therefore fully accounted for.

THE HEADLINE NUMBER DID NOT IMPROVE. sigma(0.0253 eV) 2.85303 b (-2.98 %) -> 2.84387 b (-3.30 %) vs the tape's 2.94078 b. Expected: the difference reflections are weak, so the total is dominated by sum reflections and by the basis question this option does not touch. An assertion pins that so it cannot be misread later as an improvement. The option is opt-in (ElasticChannel::GenerateExactDebyeWaller), never the default, and reports NotValidatedAgainstReferenceTape.

NEW LEAD, AND IT IS ON OUR SIDE. The flat ~2 % offset that remains matches in size and sign the ~10 % difference in the fitted W' itself: 5.977 /eV (tape, 300 K) vs 5.382 /eV (this crate, 296 K) after temperature scaling. Unlike the basis question this is about THIS PORT, needs no outside expertise, and is the most likely place a real defect on our side is still hiding. That is now this bead's remaining technical work, alongside item 2.

IMPLEMENTATION. coher::general::coher_general_with_per_atom_debye_waller folds exp(-2 W'_j E_tau) into each atom's amplitude, shared inner sum keeps the compound path byte-identical, wrong-length slice falls back rather than misassigning. endout::ElasticOutput::CoherentPreWeighted stops the factor being applied twice -- added as an enum variant not a flag so the decision had to be made at every match site, which immediately caught a second dispatch site in the validation reporter. crystals::debye_waller_deck_for_species gives the per-species decomposition with a test that it and the compound deck list name the same set.

Two of the new tests initially failed on MY wrong expectations, not the code: W' set to 0.05 /eV where SiC's real value is ~1.35 /eV; and the synthetic final edge treated as a reflection when it is a duplicated histogram-extension edge (the two paths weight it differently by 3.0e-4, now excluded and documented rather than papered over).

note.content:
STEP 5 DONE 2026-08-14 -- the pebble-bed wiring, the majorant re-check, and the end-to-end number this bead demanded all now exist and are measured.

WHAT THE 'MOSTLY CLOSED' CLAIM MISSED. Commit e4afd51779 added tests/htr10_graphite_thermal_scattering_pebble_bed.rs and described it as closing most of this bead, but its k-eigenvalue test was #[ignore]d and therefore never ran. Un-ignoring it exposed TWO real defects:

1. THE STATED BLOCKER WAS NOT REAL. The ignore reason was that Nuclide::from_core("C12") fails with WmpData("nuclide C12 not in WMPL container"), attributed to a gap in the embedded WMPL blob and filed as op-wqk.21 (which was never actually created -- it is absent from the store). There is no data gap: the CORE library carries natural carbon as "C0" (ENDF/B-VII.1 ZA 006000, listed as 'C-nat | 006000' in wmp-nuclide-manifest.md). tests/thermal_graphite_elastic.rs:307 already used "C0" correctly. It was a wrong nuclide name, not missing data. No op-wqk.21 is needed.

2. THE ACTUAL WIRING DEFECT, which the ignored test was hiding. With C0 in place the free-gas and bound runs returned BIT-IDENTICAL k. Root cause: Nuclide::sample_thermal had exactly ONE caller in the crate, physics::transport_csg. Neither physics::keff (collide_batched, transport_history, transport_history_tabulated) nor pebble_beds::keff_delta called it. So xs_at_energy correctly substituted the BOUND cross section -- setting collision rates -- while secondary energy and angle were still drawn free-gas. Internally inconsistent, and it admits no up-scatter, so a graphite-moderated spectrum cannot equilibrate. All five collision sites now route through the bound-atom law below the table cutoff, mirroring transport_csg / OpenMC src/thermal.cpp ThermalData::sample. sample_thermal consumes no RNG when there is no table or the neutron is above cutoff, so every non-thermal nuclide is bit-identical -- full suite 265 passed / 0 failed confirms no regression.

3. THE TEST PROBLEM WAS ALSO FAST, independently. It mirrored triso.rs's HEU dispersion (pf 0.30, 1 cm3 box, k~2.08) where neutrons are absorbed long before thermalizing, so the law was never sampled BY CONSTRUCTION and a null result was uninterpretable. Added diagnose_thermal_spectrum_reach (ignored diagnostic, homogenized infinite-medium sweep) to measure this instead of assuming it: 34.41% of 20k fission-born neutrons reach below the 4 eV cutoff after a mean 67.4 scatters. Retuned the case to pf 5e-4 (C/U-235 ~ 3.8e3, order-of-magnitude of a real HTR-10 pebble ~1e4) in a 6 cm reflective cube. Sensitivity is real and was measured: at pf 5e-3 the comparison has no power at all (0.20 sigma).

MEASURED RESULTS (2026-08-14, release, this environment):
  - graphite_thermal_scattering_changes_pebble_bed_keff PASSES. Free-gas C-nat k = 1.08838 +/- 0.01851; bound graphite k = 1.95254 +/- 0.01407; separation 37 sigma (dk = 0.86416, combined sigma 0.02325), 300 particles / 8 inactive + 15 active, ~107 s. Confirming run at 800 particles / 10 + 25: 1.07579 +/- 0.00833 vs 1.94166 +/- 0.00626, 83 sigma, ~410 s. Direction is physically sensible -- the bound law holds a Maxwellian near 0.025 eV where U-235 fission dominates, while the free-gas kernel (stationary target, no up-scatter) lets neutrons slide below thermal into parasitic 1/v capture. This is the gap between a CORRECT and an INCORRECT treatment of the same system, not a design change.
  - MAJORANT RE-CHECK, which this bead's coordinator note explicitly demanded be measured and not assumed (a Woodcock majorant that under-bounds Sigma_t is a SILENT BIAS, not a crash): majorant_still_bounds_total_xs_with_bound_graphite PASSES. Worst Sigma_t/Sigma_maj = 0.909091 over 200k log-spaced points from 1e-4 to 4.2 eV across both materials -- exactly 1/1.1, i.e. the sampling grid captures the true per-bin peak and the entire 10% margin survives even against graphite's 221-edge Bragg sawtooth.
  - Also fixed a latent race in the test helper: the regenerated-tape temp file was named from the PID only, but cargo runs these tests as threads of ONE process, so concurrent callers wrote/read/deleted the same path -- EndfParse("unexpected end of section data"). Now uses a per-call atomic counter. It was invisible while only one test used the helper.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: no benchmark comparison. The reference throughout is this workspace's own njoy port, so these are internal-consistency gates, not an independent NJOY/OpenMC-ACE oracle. The geometry is a packed cube, not HTR-10 -- reproducing HTR-10's published k-effective still needs the real geometry/composition under op-6tz.35 / op-6tz.35.1. AI-assisted draft, human review still owed. Do not describe HTR-10 neutronics as validated on the strength of this.

note.content:
FIXED 2026-08-20. Root cause was narrower than first diagnosed: only
x_ph_flash's own copy of the sub-region chain was broken. The other three
functions with an identical-looking chain in the same file (v_ph_eqm,
u_ph_eqm, s_ph_eqm) already gated their final (t_sat > 643.15 K) branch on
PRESSURE (p_mpa <= 21.9010 / <= 21.9316), matching v_tp_3u/v_tp_3x/v_tp_3y/
v_tp_3z's own doc-commented validity windows in MPa. x_ph_flash's copy alone
used TEMPERATURE-only thresholds (t_sat_kelvin <= 646.599 / <= 646.483) for
that same branch, so it could and did fire v_tp_3y outside its valid pressure
window -- confirmed exactly at the bug's own measured case (t_sat=646.503K,
p=21.906 MPa): v_tp_3u there gives v=2.6124e-3 m3/kg -> h_f=1993.29 kJ/kg
(sane), v_tp_3y gives v=3.076e-5 m3/kg -> h_f=-5.64e21 kJ/kg (the recorded
garbage). Fix: copied the already-correct pressure-gated pattern from the
other three functions into x_ph_flash (crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/
interfaces/functional_programming/ph_flash_eqm/mod.rs).

FIRST ATTEMPT, reverted: I initially replaced the WHOLE chain in all four
functions with a general-dispatcher-plus-temperature-nudge scheme
(v_tp_3(t_sat +/- eps, p), leaning on the crate's own fully-correct near-
critical `subregion()` map in backward_eqn_pt_3). That version fixed the
measured -1e21 case too (h_f=1993.07 kJ/kg, matching), and self-consistency-
checked cleanly against several points -- but it also replaced ALREADY-
correct code (the other three functions' pressure-gated final branch, which
was never broken) and introduced new regressions verified against this
crate's own reference-table tests: at t_sat=643.15 K exactly (the row the
crate's own saturation_table_260_degc_to_crit_temp_373_946_degc.rs literally
comments "very near critical point, this kinda fails bad") a tiny eps=1e-6 K
nudge landed BOTH the liquid and vapour probes on the same sub-region (a
genuine corner where several named sub-regions meet), and larger eps values
that worked there caused wrong-side jumps at other points near 21.93 MPa.
No single fixed epsilon covered both. Rather than build a more elaborate
adaptive-epsilon scheme under time pressure, I fell back to the narrower fix
above, which is a one-line-pattern-copy from code the crate's own test suite
already validates, not new numerical machinery.

VERIFIED: full library suite (cargo test --release -p tampines-steam-tables
--lib) is 959 passed, 0 failed, 13 ignored -- unchanged pass count from
before this fix (confirms no regression), and the previously-recorded
sic... I mean the previously-recorded h_f=-1e21 case now returns h_f=1993.29
kJ/kg instead. cargo check --workspace --lib --tests also clean.

REMAINING (not done, follow-up if wanted): the two SAME-ISSUE gap tests in
outram-mc-libs's triso_shell tests are unrelated to this crate; not
applicable here. The near-critical quality-formula ill-conditioning noted
during investigation (h_g - h_f -> ~0.0007 kJ/kg within ~0.6 K of Tc, making
x = (h-h_f)/(h_g-h_f) numerically enormous for any h even slightly off) is
real physics already documented in this crate's own "Known accuracy
pitfalls" (CLAUDE.md: "Region 3 backward equations lose digits within ~0.5 K
of Tc"), not a defect introduced or left by this fix -- no clamp was added,
since that would be new scope beyond the diagnosed dispatch bug.

note.content:
RUNG 1 STEP 1a COMPLETED as a code exercise, 2026-08-11. crates/outram-mc-libs/examples/htr10_fuel_zone_kinf.rs.

PROBLEM: HTR-10 fuel-zone infinite medium, run twice - kernels resolved explicitly as randomly packed spheres, then the same nuclide inventory homogenised. Atom densities straight from IAEA-TECDOC-1382 Table 4-38 (OPEN tier, part 2 line 1101). Kernel volume fraction of the fuelled zone = 8335 * (0.025/2.5)^3 = 8.335e-3.

MEASURED (main run, 400 particles/generation, 10 inactive + 40 active, RNG seed 1, packing seed 20260811, 1018 kernels of r = 0.025 cm in a reflective cube of half-width 1 cm, realized packing fraction 0.008328, T = 293.15 K, delta tracking with a bin-maximum bounding majorant):
  heterogeneous k_inf = 1.57269 +/- 0.00877
  homogenised   k_inf = 1.45189 +/- 0.00820
  delta k = -12081 +/- 1201 pcm; delta rho = -5291 +/- 526 pcm; 10.1 sigma
A smoke run at 200/8/25 gave 1.60870 +/- 0.02031 and 1.47273 +/- 0.01489, agreeing with the main run to 1.6 sigma on the heterogeneous case.

SIGN IS A PHYSICS CHECK AND IT PASSES: resolving the kernels depresses the flux inside each lump at the U-238 resonance energies, so fewer resonance absorptions per U-238 atom and k rises; homogenising removes the depression so it must come out lower. It does.

THIS IS NOT A PHYSICS RESULT AND NOT AN HTR-10 CRITICALITY RESULT:
- Thermal scattering is FREE GAS. Graphite S(alpha,beta) does not reach the transport path (crates/outram-mc-libs/src/material/thermal.rs:24-26). On a graphite-moderated thermal system this alone disqualifies the absolute number.
- It is a fuel-zone infinite medium - no shell, no dummy ball, no bed, no reflector, no leakage. NO published HTR-10 value corresponds to this problem, so the absolute k_inf cannot be compared to the literature at all.
- TRISO coatings unresolved (op-6tz.35). LOW fidelity tier (flat nu-bar, Watt chi stand-in, ~+500 pcm on Godiva). k_std is a generation-batch SEM with no inter-generation correlation correction. op-rbo and op-jis inherited.
- The delta k is NOT comparable to Wang et al.'s unit-cell biases: theirs are multigroup XS PROCESSING biases against a CE reference on the full model and run the other way (+2820 pcm for INFHOMMEDIUM). This is a CE GEOMETRIC effect on a different problem.

WHAT IT DOES ESTABLISH: the rung-1 chain runs end to end on this reactor's real materials, reproducibly from a stated seed, with a correctly signed self-shielding effect.

COST WARNING for step 1d: thermal neutrons in graphite scatter hundreds of times per history. The 400/10/40 run took roughly 20 minutes for 40,000 histories. Budget compute accordingly.

Full write-up: docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-neutronics.md section 11.

This paper closes the gap that the VTB cannot: docs/reactor-scoping/vtb-findings.md records that VTB has NO HTR-10 thermal hydraulics at all. Gao and Shi supply calculated power, temperature and flow distributions for BOTH the initial and the equilibrium core.

QUANTITATIVE TARGETS TO VALIDATE AGAINST:
- Maximum fuel temperature 1046 C at 120 percent overload. This is the headline number to reproduce.
- HTR-10 maximum fuel temperature LIMIT is 1230 C under normal and accident conditions, per the experiment specification. NOTE this is NOT the 1600 C figure that appears throughout the modular-HTR literature (including the JRC book kugeler2017vhtr) - 1600 C is the generic coated-particle retention limit, 1230 C is HTR-10 own specified limit. Do not conflate them.
- Bypass flow through the gaps between graphite components is under 10 percent of rated flow. Any bed model that ignores bypass is therefore making a 10 percent error in core flow.
- Uncertainties the paper explicitly carries into the peak fuel temperature: non-uniform burnup, power distribution deviation, manufacturing deviation of fuel elements, graphite balls mixed with fuel balls in the initial core, and heat-transfer calculation deviation. A V&V comparison that ignores these is comparing a best-estimate to a conservative number.
- Initial core contains graphite balls mixed uniformly with fuel balls to suppress excess reactivity; the equilibrium core has none. These are two DIFFERENT validation cases, not one.

Confirms the operating point already taken from the IAEA benchmark: 10 MW, 3.0 MPa, 4.3 kg/s, 700 C outlet, 250 C inlet, feedwater 104 C, steam 440 C at 4.0 MPa.

note.content:
SCOPE REFINEMENT from the maintainer, 2026-08-11: TUAS is not salt-only — it also does LIQUID METAL, even though salt was the original intent. So the boundary that matters is PHASE, not chemistry: TUAS covers LIQUIDS (molten salts and liquid metals), and GAS is the excluded phase.

That makes the ruling sharper rather than weaker. Do not read the earlier note on op-jyyp.4 as 'TUAS is for salt' — read it as 'TUAS is for liquids, and helium is not a liquid'. Adding a liquid-metal coolant to TUAS would be in scope; adding a gas arm is not, and that is why the HTR-10 helium circuit belongs in tampines.

Practical consequence for whoever implements this bead: do not try to generalise the TUAS Material enum into a phase-generic abstraction as a way of sneaking gas in. The liquid assumption is baked into the solver itself — TUAS is the Thermo-hydraulic Uniphase Advection and Convection Solver built on the Boussinesq approximation, which assumes small density variation. Helium at 3.0 MPa over a 250-700 C range varies in density by roughly a factor of two across the core, so the Boussinesq assumption does not hold for it. The exclusion is physical, not merely organisational.
note.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

note.content:
FINAL SCOPE FRAMING from the maintainer, 2026-08-11 — supersedes the two notes above, which were successively too narrow:

TUAS handles anything SINGLE-PHASE and NEARLY INCOMPRESSIBLE. That is liquids in practice — molten salts and liquid metals. An incompressible gas would technically fit the solver, but that restriction is severe enough that the maintainer explicitly does NOT want gas promised as a TUAS capability. Treat gas as out of scope for TUAS, full stop.

TAMPINES IS THE SUPERSET THAT INCLUDES TUAS. That is the architectural point and it resolves the whole question: gas support does not require widening TUAS, because tampines already sits above it and composes it alongside outram-park-fork-coolprop, tampines-steam-tables, outram-foam-basic-lib and chem-eng. Adding a gas layer at the tampines level is the natural place for it, not a workaround.

So the correct reading of this bead is not 'TUAS cannot do it, so find somewhere else'. It is 'tampines is where the superset lives, and a compressible helium circuit is a superset capability'.

Physical justification, unchanged: helium at 3.0 MPa across 250-700 C varies in density by roughly a factor of two through the core, so the nearly-incompressible assumption TUAS is built on genuinely does not hold for the HTR-10 primary circuit.

note.content:
CORRECTION 2026-08-11 — this bead understated existing progress. Maintainer: 'while marviken validation is not done, edwards is.'

VERIFIED IN CODE. Edwards-O'Brien pipe blowdown IS implemented and tested in crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/ (not in critical_flow/). tests.rs records the actual case inputs — initial enthalpy h = 9.857170e5 J/kg, pipe L = 4.096 m, D = 0.073 m, horizontal — and geometry.rs and drift_flux.rs carry Edwards-specific doc comments in the V&V style. So depressurisation-transient capability is NOT starting from zero.

WHAT op-bcg ACTUALLY SAYS, restated precisely so the two are not conflated: the false claim is in crates/tampines/src/critical_flow/, whose docs reference Moody / Zaloudek / Marviken data. Marviken is not done. Edwards is. Those are different modules and different benchmarks — do not treat op-bcg as invalidating the Edwards work.

THE REMAINING GAP FOR THIS BEAD IS STILL REAL, AND IT IS A FLUID-PHYSICS GAP, NOT A MISSING-CODE GAP. Edwards-O'Brien is a FLASHING TWO-PHASE WATER blowdown: subcooled water depressurises, flashes, and the choking is two-phase. An HTR-10 primary depressurisation is SINGLE-PHASE COMPRESSIBLE HELIUM. The drift-flux machinery Edwards validates is not the machinery a helium blowdown needs.

So the sequencing stands but the starting point is better than written:
1. Verify single-phase compressible choked flow analytically for an ideal monatomic gas (gamma = 5/3, critical pressure ratio ~0.487), which is a closed-form check.
2. Move to real-gas helium properties from outram-park-fork-coolprop.
3. Then the depressurisation transient.
The Edwards work gives a validated transient-blowdown framework to build within; it does not give helium choking for free.

implemented" for entropy in the simplified-polynomial-enthalpy branch this
crate already uses for H, so there's no CoolProp reference implementation
to port in this configuration at all. Instead: derived via Gibbs' theorem
(pure-component ideal-gas entropies at the mixture's total T,p, Cp(T) from
the SAME polynomials already verified for H) + the standard virial/mixing
corrections, anchored to an explicit ASHRAE zero-point convention (dry air
S=0 at 0C/1atm; water's constant derived via Clausius-Clapeyron from H's
own existing 0C anchor, confirmed consistent: h_w(0C)=2501 kJ/kg matches
the known latent heat of vaporization to 3 figures, now a permanent unit
test in mod.rs).

Caught a real bug during verification: first version used dry air's own
virial-corrected molar volume (+R*ln(v_a/v_a0)) mirroring CoolProp's own
volume-based formula -- but CoolProp's version evaluates the REAL ideal-gas
Helmholtz term there (density-native), while this port integrates Cp (the
CONSTANT-PRESSURE heat capacity), so the volume form silently smuggled in
a second, spurious T-dependence (v_a is proportional to T at fixed p),
breaking dS/dT=Cp/T by ~28% at 25C. Fixed by using -R*ln(p/p0) (total
pressure, Gibbs' theorem) for both air and water instead.

Verified: dS/dT=Cp/T (rigorous, model-independent thermodynamic identity)
holds to 7e-4 to 1.2e-3 across T=1-40C, W=0-0.02 kg/kg -- small, smooth,
and of the same order as the virial correction's own size (consistent with
a residual virial-cross-term path-dependence artifact, not a remaining bug).
CAVEAT, documented in the module doc: S's absolute value is NOT verified
against CoolProp or an external table (different reference-state convention
than CoolProp's own, and H's own mixture value already has a known ~6.6
kJ/kg ASHRAE offset that S likely inherits) -- only the temperature
dependence is rigorously verified. Full crate suite (241+ lib tests, 10 in
humid_air_reference.rs) passes; docs/api.md regenerated.

Remaining open in this bead: absolute-value cross-check for S against a
real external reference, if/when op-kbc.3 (rfluids oracle) lands.

note.content:
INVESTIGATED 2026-08-20, ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG. This bead's own text
already flagged the number as "NOT QUANTIFIED... do not treat as established
until someone measures it against the published table" -- I did that
measurement and it contradicts the bead.

I implemented the described fix (use p_sat(T) instead of p_boundary_2_3(T)
as the Region2/Region3 split for 623.15 K <= T < T_c = 647.096 K) and it
FAILS the crate's own reference-table tests. Concretely, at T=633.15 K,
p=18 MPa (a real row from the crate's single_phase_table_180_bar fixture,
p between B23(633.15K)=17.663 MPa and p_sat(633.15K)=18.666 MPa -- i.e.
exactly the band this bead claims is misclassified):

  - ORIGINAL code (uses B23 as the sole boundary): region = Region3,
    cp_tp_3(633.15K, 18MPa) = 15.82... kJ/kgK, matching the published
    reference table to within the test's 1e-3 relative tolerance (PASSES).
  - "FIXED" code (uses p_sat as the boundary below T_c): region = Region2,
    cp_tp_2(633.15K, 18MPa) = 15.860417 kJ/kgK, off by ~0.25% -- FAILS the
    same test, plus 5 more single_phase_table tests at 180-220 bar covering
    the same near-critical pressure band (all reverted cleanly by
    `git checkout` on this file; 11/11 single_phase_table_20_bar_to_220_bar
    tests pass again with the original B23-only logic restored).

So the physical picture in my "fix" was backwards. B23(T) rises SLOWER than
p_sat(T) as T increases from 623.15 K (they coincide exactly at 623.15 K,
16.529 MPa, then diverge: at 633.15 K, B23=17.663 MPa < p_sat=18.666 MPa).
The sliver between them is evidently still correctly Region 3 per IAPWS-IF97
-- B23 is not simply "the true saturation curve, valid only above Tc" as I
assumed; it is IF97's own chosen practical boundary between the Region 2 and
Region 3 backward-equation domains at every T from 623.15 K up, independent
of where the true two-phase dome sits. My reasoning that "Region 1 doesn't
extend above 623.15 K, so anything above p_sat there must be Region 3, and
therefore Region 2 must stop at p_sat too" does not follow -- IAPWS clearly
intends a band of single-phase vapour (still below the true p_sat) to be
evaluated with Region 3's equations instead of Region 2's, for accuracy
reasons this bead's author did not have when writing the original diagnosis.

CLOSING as investigated / not a defect. region_fwd_eqn_single_phase's
original code is reverted to unchanged and is correct as far as this
crate's own reference-table coverage can show. If a future reader has an
IAPWS-IF97 citation showing an actual bug in the B23-only dispatch, reopen
with that citation and a specific counter-example row, not a re-derivation
from first principles the way this bead's original text did.

note.content:
CORRECTION + REAL EVIDENCE from maintainer, 2026-08-13 07:2x. Supersedes the 'low temperature / ambient / cold start' inference in the original description -- that was WRONG.

ACTUAL FAILURE:
  htgr-physics failed in helium primary loop (circulator + hot gas duct)
  (crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/array_control_vol_and_fluid_component_collections/one_d_solid_array_with_lateral_coupling/calculation.rs:95:81):
  called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: ThermophysicalPropertyTemperatureRangeError

'Low temp' in the maintainer's phrasing means ~700+ degC -- i.e. LOW relative to the HTGR envelope, but it is the correlation's UPPER validity bound that is being exceeded. The solid material's range tops out around 700 degC and the hot gas duct / circulator solid nodes run past it.

TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS HERE -- fix both, do not conflate:

(1) RANGE TOO NARROW (the physics fix, = op-x0v1).
    The steel correlation in use tops out near 700 degC. HTGR hot-leg helium is ~750-950 degC depending on the plant, so the range is simply unfit for this application. Needs sourced properties to 1200 degC. Confirm the exact current bound and which SolidMaterial variant is selected for the hot gas duct.

(2) UNWRAP ON A RECOVERABLE ERROR (the robustness fix, TUAS).
    calculation.rs:95 `.unwrap()`s a Result whose Err variant is a normal, anticipatable out-of-range condition. That converts a diagnosable property-range error into a panic that takes down the whole sim and reports no temperature, no node, and no material. Propagate the error (or at minimum surface WHICH material, WHICH node, and WHAT temperature was requested vs the allowed range) instead of unwrapping.
    This is worth fixing even after the range is widened -- the next material to go out of range should produce a usable message, not a bare panic.

Check whether the same unwrap pattern appears elsewhere in one_d_solid_array_with_lateral_coupling/ and its fluid-array siblings.
