note.content:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED, 2026-08-13 07:3x (read from source; panic not re-run -- htgr_sim_v1 is an egui GUI example with no headless mode yet, see op-szmi.3).

THE NUMBER: SolidMaterial::SteelSS304L is tabulated to a MAX of 1000 K = 726.85 degC.
  crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/boussinesq_thermophysical_properties/solid_database/ss_304_l.rs:705-712
    max_temp_ss_304l_zou_zweibaum_spline() -> 1000 K
    min_temp_ss_304l_zou_zweibaum_spline() ->  250 K
  Bounds are enforced by range_check() in .../boussinesq_thermophysical_properties/mod.rs:239, which returns
  TuasLibError::ThermophysicalPropertyTemperatureRangeError. That is the Err that gets unwrapped.

WHY IT BITES htgr_sim_v1 SO EASILY -- the margin is 27 K:
  HTR-10 phase-1 published core outlet = 700 degC = 973.15 K
    (crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/htr10/design.rs:118, helium_outlet_phase1)
  SS304L ceiling                       = 726.85 degC = 1000 K
  => ~26.85 K of headroom at the NOMINAL design point. Any transient overshoot exits the range.
  HTR-10 phase 2 (900 degC outlet) would be ~173 K OUTSIDE the range and cannot be modelled at all today.

THE PANICKING CALL SITE:
  one_d_solid_array_with_lateral_coupling/calculation.rs:95
    .map(|&temperature| try_get_rho_cp(material, temperature, pressure).unwrap())
  Inside a closure in an iterator chain, which is why it is an unwrap and not a  -- fixing it means
  collecting into Result<Array1<_>, _> (collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?) rather than just swapping the operator.
  The reported column is :95:81, which matches the .unwrap() on that line.

THE CONSUMER: the steam generator's tube metal is SolidMaterial::SteelSS304L
  (examples/htgr_sim_v1/physics/primary_loop.rs:481, in steam_generator_config()).
  The 'circulator + hot gas duct' label is the stage marker at physics/mod.rs:313; the primary step owns
  the steam generator, so the failing SolidColumn is the SG TUBE METAL, not a duct wall.

THIS CEILING IS ALREADY A KNOWN, DOCUMENTED CONSTRAINT -- the code works around it rather than fixing it:
  - physics/mod.rs:556-577 -- the whole-plant smoke test asserts metal stays below 1000 K, and records that a
    50% rod bank insertion 'dies at 6 s when the tube metal passes SteelSS304L's 1000 K ceiling and TUAS panics'.
  - physics/primary_loop.rs:1286-1330 -- core_inlet_responds_to_secondary_heat_removal deliberately throttles to
    2.2 kg/s instead of 1.0 kg/s BECAUSE 1.0 kg/s 'drives the tube metal through the steel limit and kills the run'.
  So a test was weakened to stay inside this range. Widening the range should let that test go back to 1.0 kg/s --
  check that when the properties land.

SECOND CEILING NEARBY (do not lose it): IF97 stops at 1073.15 K, per the same docs. Widening the steel range
alone will not make an excursion survivable; it moves the failure to the steam side. Note it, do not fix it here.

note.content:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-11 (this session; AI-assisted draft, NOT human-reviewed, NOT committed - coordinator holds the diff).

WHAT LANDED
- crates/outram-mc-libs/src/material/thermal.rs: new pub enum ThermalElastic {None, Coherent(CoherentElasticTable), Incoherent(IncoherentElasticTable)} (enum dispatch, no trait objects/Box/lifetimes). ThermalScattering now owns an elastic channel alongside the inelastic one, with elastic_xs(E), total_xs(E) and elastic() accessors. from_endf_file() reads the ENDF tape ONCE and DETECTS the elastic law from the evaluation (MT=2 LTHR=1/3 -> coherent, LTHR=2/3 -> incoherent, absent -> None); its signature is unchanged so every existing caller is source-compatible. NjoyError::NotPorted from a channel constructor is treated as 'this evaluation has no such section'; every other error, notably TemperatureOutOfRange, is propagated rather than silently dropping graphite's dominant channel.
- ThermalScattering::sample() now splits elastic vs inelastic with probability sigma_el/sigma_thermal, mirroring OpenMC src/thermal.cpp:296-302 ThermalData::sample_dist. The coherent branch mirrors src/secondary_thermal.cpp:34-54 CoherentElasticAE::sample (invert the cumulative structure factor, mu = 1 - 2 E_k/E, E_out = E_in).
- COHERENT IS STORED EXACTLY, NOT RESAMPLED. sigma_coh_el(E) is a 1/E sawtooth with 221 discontinuities for graphite, so a log-grid resample would smear every Bragg edge. CoherentElasticTable holds the Bragg-edge table itself (221 (E,sigma) pairs, ~3.5 kB - cheaper than the resample AND exact). Incoherent elastic IS resampled (it is smooth); grid sized by measurement at 400 points.
- crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/src/thermr/scattering.rs: added CoherentElasticScattering::bragg_edge_table() -> Vec<(NeutronEnergy, CrossSection)>, the uom-typed accessor that makes the exact storage possible. Mirrors the OpenMC CoherentElasticXS::bragg_edges()/factors() pair. This is the ONLY njoy-side change; the data/transport boundary is intact (outram-mc still parses no ENDF).
- crates/outram-mc-libs/src/material/nuclide.rs: xs_at_energy's thermal substitution now swaps in th.total_xs(e) = sigma_inel + sigma_el, not sigma_inel alone. THIS IS THE ACTUAL DEFECT THIS BEAD NAMED.

MEASURED (ENDF/B-VIII.0, release mode, 2026-08-11; full methodology + results in the module header of crates/outram-mc-libs/tests/thermal_graphite_elastic.rs, 7 tests, all green)
- Graphite MAT 30, 296 K, barn per carbon atom at 0.0253 eV: sigma_coh_el 4.5514, sigma_inel 0.4863, elastic fraction 0.9035. Confirms the ~90 % figure this bead was filed on.
- Exactness: worst relative deviation of the stored Bragg table vs the njoy surface = 7.67e-16 over 21199 points spanning 1e-4 to 4 eV. Bragg cutoff 1.822327e-3 eV (graphite (002)); sigma_el exactly 0.0 below it.
- Nuclide-level, C0 + graphite table vs bare C0, MicroXS::elastic at 0.0253 eV: free-gas 4.9398, bound-new 5.0378, bound-OLD (inel only) 0.4863. The pre-fix path gave graphite 9.8 % of its free-gas scattering; the fixed path gives 102.0 %.
- Sampling, 200000 draws at 0.0253 eV seed 1: elastic fraction 0.90340 vs cross-section prediction 0.90346 (0.09 sigma on a 6.6e-4 binomial sigma). Mean Bragg cosine -0.02357 vs the analytic sum p_i mu_i = -0.02497 over the 17 open reflections (1.17 sigma on SEM 1.20e-3).
- HTR-10 temperatures at 0.0253 eV: 293.15 K snaps to 296 K (NJOY tolerance) -> 4.5514/0.4863; 393.15 K interpolated -> 4.3849/0.6779; 523.15 K interpolated -> 4.1672/0.9445; 1073.15 K interpolated -> 3.3592/2.0373. Monotone Debye-Waller suppression; 100 K and 2200 K are hard TemperatureOutOfRange refusals.
- LIGHT-WATER REGRESSION: tsl-HinH2O MAT 1 at 293.6 K reports channel 'none', sigma_el identically 0, total_xs == inelastic_xs bit-identical, sigma_inel(0.0253) = 52.1420 b. The existing thermal pincell case is unaffected.

note.content:
Stagnation inflow BC now EXERCISED AND VERIFIED for the single-phase subcooled steady path, 2026-08-11 (~17:00 SGT). Items 2, 3, 4 of this bead are done; item 1 (land vs hold) stays a maintainer decision.

NEW TEST: reservoir_inlet_reaches_the_bernoulli_limit_in_subcooled_water in crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/tests.rs (+~390 lines incl. V&V doc). Closed form derived from the DISCRETE steady state of the scheme's own momentum balances (not the continuum limit): p0 - p_out = rho u^2/2 + rho F L with Darcy F, giving u = sqrt(2 dp / (rho (1 + f L/D))), friction incorporated (not neglected) via the code's own laminar-64/Re / Blasius closure. Case: p0 1.000 MPa -> p_out 0.980 MPa, T 300 K (~153 K subcooled), L 0.5 m, D 0.1 m, 20 cells, dt 0.5 ms, 3000 steps; all solver knobs at defaults.

MEASURED: closed-form u 6.225884 m/s vs measured steady inlet u 6.225891 m/s -> relative error +1.12e-6 against a 1.0 % tolerance PRE-COMMITTED in the doc comment before the first run (a-priori budget ~0.1 %, gated 10x looser because reference f is evaluated once at (p_out, mu_f)). Frictionless Bernoulli would be 6.334222 m/s; measured sits 1.7102 % below, matching the friction correction. Continuity |mdot_in - mdot_out|/mdot 1.28e-6; steadiness 3.3e-7; max Courant 0.125; alpha = 0 exactly throughout; ~6-7 s wall clock. Strongest evidence: the three pressure terms match INDIVIDUALLY (p[0] 980661.291 predicted vs 980661.29 measured; interior drop 644.376 vs 644.33; outflow face 16.957 vs 16.96), separately confirming the conservative half-cell inlet convection, the half-cell Dirichlet coefficient dt/(rho dx/2), and friction charged over exactly L. No defect found; the non-conservative alternative the BC doc warns about would sit at ~4.48 m/s (-28 %) and nothing near that appears.

DOCS: AxialBoundary::ReservoirInlet public doc now states both standing assumptions (zero inlet drift velocity; infinite non-depleting plenum) plus a V&V status block — doc-comment-only edits to drift_flux.rs, no code/signature/constant changed.

ALSO EXERCISED INDIRECTLY: the Marviken gates (op-ja3t) drive this BC through 897 marched two-phase transients with 0 refused steps.

STILL UNVERIFIED (stated in the test doc and the ReservoirInlet V&V block): two-phase inflow (InflowState::void_fraction and rho_g never exercised, alpha = 0 throughout the direct test), the h0 - u^2/2 static-enthalpy split only probed at 2e-4 relative head, backflow through either boundary, and transient behaviour. upwind_scalar has no direct unit test — it is private to drift_flux and tests.rs is a sibling module, so it needs a pub(super) visibility change first; filed as a follow-up bead (see op tracker, filed today). Note also Blasius is applied at Re ~ 4.1e6, beyond its nominal ~1e5 range — a property of the code under test, reproduced not corrected. Not closing this bead — maintainer decision.

note.content:
DETECTION METHOD, added 2026-08-11. Item (4), the character-corrupted Sod appendix, is caught automatically by the workspace's own mandated README check:

  pandoc -f gfm+tex_math_dollars -t html --mathml <file> > /dev/null

It reports: [WARNING] Could not convert TeX math p / \*ho^\gamma = \text{const}. That is a corrupted \rho.

A full sweep of all 118 git-tracked README.md files on 2026-08-11 with pandoc 3.6.1 produced exactly ONE warning across the whole workspace, and it was this file. Every other README, including the ten that carry LaTeX math, converts cleanly with zero warnings and exit 0. So this is the sole outstanding markdown defect in the repository, which makes it cheap to confirm fixed later — re-run the sweep and expect zero warnings.

CONFIRMING THE BEAD'S OWN WARNING against a fresh look: automated repair really is unsafe. The file contains 160 '*' characters. Legitimate ones are the star-state notation (\rho^*_L, \rho^*_R, pStar) and ordinary markdown emphasis; corrupted ones are single characters substituted at random positions. Observed substitutions include a space in 'rarefaction*relation' and 'a*Riemann', 'i' in 'rarefaction *s' and 'rat*o', 'r' in '\*ho' and '*atio', 's' in 'post-*hock', a backslash in '\sqrt{*gamma', 'n' in 'ha*dy', 'o' in '*f', 'c' in 'post-rarefa*tion', and an underscore in '\rho^**L'. The replaced characters follow no pattern, so there is no rule that separates corruption from notation. Hand restoration against Toro (2013) remains the only safe route.

Only the pandoc-visible math error is machine-detectable; the corrupted PROSE is invisible to every automated check, so a clean pandoc run after a partial fix would NOT mean the appendix is restored.

DESIGN AGREED WITH MAINTAINER 2026-08-12 -- bake to a texture, tint at draw.

Key enabling fact: triso_dot_offset is deterministic by construction (htr10_reactor_vessel.rs:431 documents this explicitly -- it exists to stop the speckle shimmering between frames). The artwork is therefore STATIC across frames. Re-drawing it every repaint is pure waste, not animation.

Do NOT snapshot the finished coloured picture -- temperature changes every frame and would invalidate the cache immediately, buying nothing.

Instead: rasterise the depth-shaded bed ONCE into an egui ColorImage as luminance/alpha, upload via ctx.load_texture, and paint it as a SINGLE textured quad with the temperature colour applied as a multiply tint. Temperature then never invalidates the cache. Per-frame cost goes from ~10000 circles to 4 vertices.

Fill level composes as a CLIP RECT at draw time, not a cache key -- bake the full bed, clip to the fill line.

Cache key: physical pixel size (rect * pixels_per_point), so it re-bakes only on resize or DPI/monitor change.

Cheaper half-measure if the texture route stalls: cache a pre-tessellated egui::Mesh. Skips CPU tessellation but still uploads ~120k vertices per frame. Strictly worse; note it only as a fallback.

Known tradeoff to accept or mitigate: a texture is raster and will resample on resize where the current vector path stays crisp. Keying the bake on PHYSICAL pixels avoids this in the steady state.

Still do the measurement first (promote GuiFrameMetrics to src/app_scaffold/) so the before/after is a number, not a claim.

2026-08-17: option (a) is now available and MEASURED. The maintainer committed the official ENDF/B-VIII.0 tsl-CinSiC tape (MAT 44, 7.2 MB, commit ffef0fb76f); it now lives at reference-data/endf/tsl-CinSiC.endf after op-mixd moved tapes out of crates/.

The tape carries MF=7/MT=2 LTHR=1: 685 Bragg edges over 8 temperatures. Read through the existing SabSource::EndfTape path (no new physics needed), measured at 0.0253 eV / 296 K, barn per principal atom:

  C in SiC, regenerated from deck : elastic 0.00000 + inelastic 0.13291 = 0.13291  (free-gas C0 4.9382 -> -97.3%)
  C in SiC, from the committed tape: elastic 2.94078 + inelastic 0.13880 = 3.07957  (free-gas C0 4.9382 -> -37.6%)
  C in graphite, for scale         : elastic 4.55142 + inelastic 0.48634 = 5.03776
  Bragg cutoff, C in SiC: 1.066463e-3 eV (graphite: 1.822327e-3 eV)

So the tape gives 23x the total thermal cross section the deck path gives, and the -37.6% bound-vs-free figure is physically plausible where -97.3% was not.

NOT YET DONE, so this bead stays open:
  - The two GAP tests in outram-mc-libs/tests/triso_shell_thermal_scattering.rs still assert elastic == 0.0. They are designed to fail when the gap closes; they have not been flipped, because nothing yet routes the SiC layer at the tape.

  - geometry/triso_particle.rs module doc still records the limitation.

MAINTAINER DIRECTION 2026-08-17: option (b) -- implement the Zhu and Hawari generalized coherent-elastic formulation in coher.rs -- was chosen over wiring the tape alone, so the capability is wanted regardless. Prerequisite: neither Zhu 2014 (MS thesis, NCSU) nor Zhu and Hawari 2015 (ICNC) is in crates/kovan-literature; per the workspace literature HARD RULE they must be catalogued before their formulation is used. The committed tsl-CinSiC MT=2 (685 edges, 8 temperatures) is then a real published oracle to validate the implementation against, and reproducing the six built-in NJOY lattices through the general path is a second free gate.
note.author: root@vm

note.content:
2026-08-17 (2): the silicon half is now supplied too (op-84v6). Both SiC tapes live in reference-data/endf/. Measured at 0.0253 eV / 296 K, barn per principal atom:

  C in SiC  (MAT 44): elastic 2.94078 + inelastic 0.13880 = 3.07957  (free-gas C 4.9382 -> -37.6%)
  Si in SiC (MAT 43): elastic 2.94078 + inelastic 0.06615 = 3.00693  (free-gas Si-28 1.9914 -> +51.0%)

CRITICAL for wiring: those two elastic figures are identical because MAT 43 and MAT 44 carry byte-identical MF=7/MT=2 sections (1044 records each; only the header ZA/AWR differs). Coherent elastic is a lattice property of 3C-SiC, not a per-sublattice one. So summing the elastic channels of both materials double-counts Bragg scattering -- MT=2 must be attributed to the compound once. This is a real trap: it would give a plausible wrong k rather than a crash, the same failure mode this bead was opened about.

Also: the evaluator's tsl-SiinSiC.readme (shipped with the tape, now in reference-data/endf/) states in its own words that the coherent elastic 'was generated using an in-house routine [1]', citing Zhu and Hawari, ICNC 2015. That is independent corroboration of this bead's root-cause analysis, from the evaluation itself rather than inferred from card 4's iel=0.

Still open, unchanged: the two GAP tests in outram-mc-libs/tests/triso_shell_thermal_scattering.rs still assert elastic == 0.0 (they test the DECK path, which remains correctly elastic-free); nothing yet routes the SiC layer at the tapes; and the maintainer's chosen path is option (b), implementing the Zhu-Hawari generalized formulation, for which the two papers are still not in kovan-literature.

note.content:
One addition to this surface, 2026-08-11 (uncommitted), made while implementing op-nhoa: CoherentElasticScattering::bragg_edge_table() -> Vec<(NeutronEnergy, CrossSection)>, one uom-typed pair per tabulated Bragg edge (221 for ENDF/B-VIII.0 crystalline graphite), where sigma_i = S(E_i,T)/(E_i*natom) is the value cross_section() takes throughout [E_i, E_{i+1}).

WHY IT WAS NEEDED: sigma_coh_el(E) is a 1/E sawtooth with a discontinuity at every edge. A consumer that pre-tabulates it on its own log grid - which outram-mc must do, to keep the transport hot loop cheap - smears all 221 edges. Exposing the step table lets the consumer cache the channel EXACTLY instead: measured worst relative deviation of outram-mc's cached copy vs this surface is 7.67e-16 over 21199 points from 1e-4 to 4 eV, and the whole table is ~3.5 kB, cheaper than the resample it replaces. Everything else (the cumulative structure factor S_i/natom = sigma_i*E_i, and each edge's sampling weight as its increment) is recoverable from the pairs exactly.

It mirrors the CoherentElasticXS::bragg_edges() / ::factors() pair that OpenMC's CoherentElasticAE::sample consumes (src/secondary_thermal.cpp:34-54), so it is a port move rather than an invention. No behaviour change to any existing method. njoy full suite green after it (393 lib tests + all integration, scripts/test.sh, release). Not closing - human review still owed on this bead's original work too.

RECOMMENDATION, not a decision -- flagging this as a genuine blocker for the maintainer rather than deciding unilaterally, per the criteria that make it different from op-6ez3/op-9bvi (which I did decide): this one (a) changes a persisted on-disk schema (DATASET_SCHEMA_VERSION bump, PlotCalibration becomes an enum with a new variant) affecting every previously-exported dataset's re-readability, and (b) blocks nothing else in the op-9c2e tree today -- the axis-aligned persistent draggable box (op-zfnh, shipped) already solves the bulk of the practical complaint (no more one-click-per-corner), and per the bead's own description a parallelogram variant would coexist with, not replace, axis-aligned calibration.

My recommendation, for whenever the maintainer wants to pick this up: enum-dispatch per the workspace's no-trait-objects rule --

  pub enum PlotCalibration {
      AxisAligned(AxisCalibration, AxisCalibration),  // today's shape, renamed as a variant
      Parallelogram { corners: [PixelPoint; 4], data_corners: [(f64, f64); 4] },
  }

with point_at() matching on the variant (axis-aligned: today's per-axis linear/log interpolation, unchanged; parallelogram: a bilinear or full 2D projective (homography) map from the pixel quadrilateral to the data-space quadrilateral -- projective is the more correct choice if the plot was genuinely photographed at an angle with perspective foreshortening, bilinear is simpler and adequate for a merely-skewed-but-not-perspective scan). DATASET_SCHEMA_VERSION -> 2, with read_json handling both old (implicit AxisAligned) and new records for backward read compatibility -- write path always emits the new shape.

Not implemented. Left open pending maintainer input on: (1) is this worth the schema churn given op-zfnh already shipped, (2) bilinear vs full projective, (3) whether AxisAligned stays the default/only option for existing UX and Parallelogram is opt-in via a toggle, or whether the draggable box should just always be a freely-skewable quadrilateral (simpler UI, but changes existing muscle memory for the common axis-aligned case).

note.content:
COLORBREWER SOURCE CLARIFICATION (checked 2026-08-06, prompted by the maintainer asking whether github.com/axismaps/colorbrewer is 'the' ColorBrewer):

Yes -- axismaps/colorbrewer is the official repository behind colorbrewer2.org, maintained by Axis Maps, with the schemes based on Dr Cynthia Brewer's research.

BUT THE TWO LICENCE FILES ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE:
  - github.com/axismaps/colorbrewer/LICENCE.txt is the STOCK Apache-2.0 boilerplate with the placeholders left unfilled ('Copyright {yyyy} {name of copyright owner}'). It names no copyright holder and carries no acknowledgement clause. It governs Axis Maps' website/software.
  - colorbrewer2.org/export/LICENSE.txt is Apache-2.0 WITH the copyright filled in -- (c) 2002 Cynthia Brewer, Mark Harrower, The Pennsylvania State University -- and the specific condition that end-user documentation acknowledge: 'This product includes color specifications and designs developed by Cynthia Brewer (http://colorbrewer.org/)'. It also forbids using the ColorBrewer name to endorse derivatives.

The colour SPECIFICATIONS are the part this project would use, so the export licence is the authoritative one to cite. Taking the GitHub boilerplate instead would mean redistributing the colour data with no named copyright holder and no attribution -- the same defect as taking them via Panoply.

Unchanged recommendation: Crameri's Scientific colour maps (MIT, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1243862) remain the simpler choice, with no attribution clause to carry and better suitability for scientific data. ColorBrewer stays viable if its acknowledgement is honoured in user-facing docs.
note.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop

note.content:
DECIDED 2026-08-06 (maintainer): use CRAMERI'S SCIENTIFIC COLOUR MAPS. ColorBrewer is not being adopted; the licence comparison above is retained only as the record of why.

Licence: MIT. Verified on the Zenodo record, v8.0.1, published 2023-10-05.
Cite: Crameri, F. (2018). Scientific colour maps. Zenodo. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1243862
Home: https://www.fabiocrameri.ch/colourmaps/  Supporting paper: Geoscientific Model Development (2018).
MIT is compatible with this workspace's GPL-3.0-only and carries no attribution clause to thread through user-facing docs.

WHY CRAMERI RATHER THAN COLORBREWER (the reason is technical, not preference):
ColorBrewer's schemes were designed to make DISCRETE choropleth classes distinguishable and are NOT perceptually uniform. Stretched across a continuous field they manufacture apparent banding -- fast-changing stretches read as steep gradients and flat stretches as isothermal, when the underlying data is smooth. For widgets whose stated premise is that rendering derives directly from physics state, a colour map that invents structure is actively wrong. Crameri's are perceptually uniform by construction: equal steps in the quantity read as equal steps in colour.

Two further properties that matter here:
  - Greyscale-safe: stays readable printed black-and-white, which the V&V write-ups will need.
  - CYCLIC maps (romaO, vikO, ...). ColorBrewer has no equivalent, and the turbine rotor angle is a cyclic quantity -- a cyclic map is the correct way to colour one.

ColorBrewer's qualitative sets remain the more battle-tested option IF categorical palettes are ever wanted (flow regimes, component types, material IDs). Revisit only for that.

MAP SELECTION (suggested, confirm when implementing):
  - temperature / hot-cold, diverging: vik or roma
  - sequential (quality, burnup, flux): lajolla, lipari, or batlow
  - cyclic (rotor angle, phase): romaO or vikO

IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINTS (unchanged):
  - ADD alongside the existing maps; never replace them. crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/color_maps/ is documented as already-validated code whose exact values call sites depend on. hot_to_cold_colour_mark_1 and steam_quality_colour_mark_1 both stay.
  - Provenance header on the new module (project, author, version, DOI, licence, URL, date accessed) plus a References.md entry, per RESEARCH_INTEGRITY_AND_PROVENANCE.md.
  - Vendor only the specific map tables used, with their MIT notice, rather than the whole suite.
  - Callers that would benefit: PipeVisual cell fills, TurbineVisual casing, the per-stage steam-quality tint.

note.content:
SCOPE WIDENED by maintainer, 2026-08-13: the properties must be usable inside htgr_sim_v1, and the sim is currently CRASHING AT LOW TEMPERATURES (see op-m1jz, P1).

So this is no longer a high-temperature-only ask. The needed validity range spans ambient (~20-25 degC) through 1200 degC in one continuous, non-panicking correlation set. When selecting sources and correlations, check the LOW end explicitly -- that is what is breaking today; 1200 degC is the headroom requirement.
note.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

note.content:
CORRECTION, 2026-08-13 07:2x -- disregard the previous note claiming the LOW end (ambient) is what breaks. That was my wrong inference. Real trace is on op-m1jz.

The actual failure is the UPPER bound: the solid steel correlation used by htgr_sim_v1's hot gas duct / circulator tops out around 700 degC and throws ThermophysicalPropertyTemperatureRangeError above it. HTGR hot-leg helium runs ~750-950 degC, so the existing range is unfit for purpose.

So this bead is back to being exactly what it said originally -- HIGH-temperature properties, to 1200 degC -- and it is now on the critical path for a P1 crash rather than being forward-looking headroom. Priority raised accordingly.

The specific consumer to satisfy first: whichever SolidMaterial variant htgr_sim_v1 assigns to the hot gas duct and circulator.

Delivered in crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/ldu_matrix/parallel.rs (+ parallel/tests.rs), declared from ldu_matrix/mod.rs:
- HybridLdu: spmv/spmv_into, residual/residual_into, normalised_residual, diagonal_reciprocal(_into), auto_backend, with_matrix.
- LduTopology: the cell-gather (CRS) inversion of the face addressing.

Strategy: cell-gather reformulation, parallel over cells, so each output is written by exactly one thread. Per-cell face lists are stored in ascending face order, which makes the product BITWISE IDENTICAL to LduMatrix::multiply on every backend and at any thread count (verified by to_bits comparison, and at 1/2/4/8 threads). Reductions use fixed 1024-element blocks combined in block order, so they are bitwise identical across backends too, though not to the flat sums in krylov::vecops.

- SpMV crossover ~4096 cells (1.04x/1.02x over two runs); loses at 1728 (0.55x/0.65x); 2.5-3.5x from 32768 cells up. SPMV_MIN_CELLS = 4096, which SUPPORTS the crate-wide CPU_MULTI_MIN_WORK_ITEMS placeholder of 4096 for this kernel.

note.content: Maintainer decision, 2026-08-12: f32 on the GPU is ACCEPTED for now. Do not block this epic on f64 GPU support or on the op-0nh Faddeeva f32 accuracy review. Requirement is a DOCUMENTED CAVEAT, not a fix: every GPU kernel's doc comment must state (a) the precision it actually runs at, (b) the measured max/RMS deviation from the f64 serial CPU oracle on the stated test problem, and (c) that the GPU path is therefore not the reference result. The parity-gate tolerances are set to pass at f32 deliberately -- that is the maintainer's call, not a loosened tolerance of convenience. note.content:
MEASURED CROSSOVER for the field-algebra kernels (fields::parallel), 2026-08-12, 4 logical cores, --release --features parallel.

FINDING: compute::CPU_MULTI_MIN_WORK_ITEMS = 4096 is FAR TOO LOW for these kernels. It is a placeholder I wrote without measurement, and measuring it shows it would make callers SLOWER, not faster.

c = a + b, best of 9 after 2 warm-ups, --test-threads=1, least-contended of 10 sweeps:

  n          serial      CpuMulti    speedup
  1024       0.43 us     7.59 us     0.06x
  4096       1.89 us     11.07 us    0.17x   <-- at the current placeholder: ~6x SLOWER
  16384      5.99 us     23.11 us    0.26x
  65536      56.27 us    30.39 us    1.85x
  131072     117.77 us   49.87 us    2.36x
  262144     239.65 us   89.52 us    2.68x
  1048576    2001.64 us  437.34 us   4.58x

Cause: these kernels are memory-bandwidth bound at 1-2 flops/element, so thread overhead dominates far longer than for compute-dense work.

THE CROSSOVER IS A BAND, NOT A POINT. Shared virtualised host: serial repeatable to <5%, parallel varies up to 4x run to run. Win counts over 10 sweeps: <=16384 -> 0/10; 65536 -> 4/10; 131072 -> 6/10; 262144 -> 9/10; 1048576 -> 10/10. Honest statement: crossover lies between 65536 and 262144 on this host and cannot be pinned further.

fields::parallel::field_parallel_crossover() therefore overrides the global constant at 131072 (majority winner), using the override mechanism compute.rs's own docs sanction. Losing at 131072 costs tens of microseconds; setting 262144 would forfeit a measured 1.3x-2.4x.

CAVEAT: one shared virtualised 4-core sandbox. Re-measure on real hardware before trusting 131072.

Kernel speedups at n=1048576 (representative of 4 runs): add 2.75x, axpy 2.49x, pointwise_mul 3.82x, sum 2.95x, l2_norm 2.70x, dot 2.56x, axpy_assign 3.23x. Range across runs 2.5x-4.3x.

REDUCTION DETERMINISM (relevant to this bead's parity-gate criteria): fixed-chunk tree reduction, REDUCTION_CHUNK=4096, chunks summed in index order. Bit-reproducible run to run (32/32 identical) AND identical across thread counts (pools of 1,2,3,4,7,8 all bitwise equal). NOT bit-equal to Serial: measured worst-case relative deviation 7.857e-14 (vol_integral); sum 5.690e-14, dot 7.189e-15, l2_norm 6.785e-15. Asserted tolerance 1e-11. min/max ARE bit-identical to serial. Element-wise kernels are bit-identical to Serial on every backend and size.

GPU: no field kernel exists; ComputeBackend::Gpu routes to the best CPU path, documented rather than silently pretended. The Serial-vs-Gpu half of this bead's parity gate is therefore still entirely open for this module.

note.content:
MEASURED CROSSOVERS for the LDU kernels (ldu_matrix::parallel), 2026-08-12, available_parallelism()=4, release --features parallel, idle machine.

HEADLINE: there must NOT be one crate-wide CPU_MULTI_MIN_WORK_ITEMS. The two kernel families measured so far want thresholds 64x apart, and a single number is wrong for at least one of them.

SpMV, time per call, best of 7 samples, two independent runs:

  cells     serial      CpuMulti    speedup   repeat
  1000      20.24 us    20.08 us    1.01x     1.00x
  1728      34.55 us    63.28 us    0.55x     0.65x
  2744      55.67 us    69.32 us    0.80x     1.21x
  4096      83.67 us    80.61 us    1.04x     1.02x   <-- break-even
  8000      165.60 us   114.06 us   1.45x     2.02x
  32768     690.40 us   277.86 us   2.48x     2.03x
  512000    13338 us    4822 us     2.77x     3.48x

For SpMV the placeholder 4096 is CORRECT -- it is precisely where the parallel path stops losing. SPMV_MIN_CELLS = 4096.

For vector ops 4096 is badly wrong: dot only wins from ~65536; axpy is still break-even at 262144 (1.87x one run, 1.00x the other) and reliable only from ~1048576. At 4096 elements axpy on 4 threads is 0.05x -- TWENTY TIMES SLOWER. VECOP_MIN_ELEMENTS = 262144.

Compare the field-algebra measurement already filed on this bead: those memory-bound kernels wanted 131072. So three kernel families, three different answers (4096 / 131072 / 262144). The right resolution for this bead is per-kernel measured constants with compute.rs's global as a floor, not a single tuned number.

THREAD SCALING, 262144 cells: 1 -> 6487 us, 2 -> 3481 us (1.86x), 4 -> 2322 us (2.79x), 8 -> 1830 us (3.54x). Output asserted BITWISE IDENTICAL at every thread count. The >3x on 4 cores is superlinear and reproducible; a cache hypothesis is documented in the code and explicitly labelled UNCONFIRMED.

PARITY (this bead's Serial-vs-CpuMulti criterion): spmv, residual, diagonal_reciprocal and axpy are BIT-FOR-BIT IDENTICAL to the serial path, not merely within tolerance -- the cell-gather stores each cell's incident faces in ascending face index, which is the order the serial scatter reaches them. Verified via to_bits() at 24/512/32768 cells, symmetric and asymmetric, at 1/2/4/8 threads. Reductions are bitwise identical across backends and thread counts but not equal to the flat krylov::vecops sums: dot worst 2.3744e-13 raw at n=4194304 (7.9476e-17 scaled by sum|a_i b_i|; the raw figure inflates because the test vectors cancel to ~150), normalised_residual 7.6520e-15 (~34 ulp), norm_l1 8.9257e-14, norm_l2 2.4996e-15.

Serial-vs-Gpu parity remains ENTIRELY OPEN for this module: there is no GPU LDU kernel, and ComputeBackend::Gpu degrades to the best CPU path (asserted in a test so it cannot silently claim the GPU).

CAVEATS: one machine, 4 cores, idle. Not measured on Android hardware or a many-core server. Under load the SpMV break-even moves right -- an earlier contended run put 4096 cells at 0.72x. norm_l1/norm_l2 were not separately benchmarked; they inherit dot's floor by assumption.

note.content:
MEASURED CROSSOVER for batched root finding (math::parallel), 2026-08-12, available_parallelism()=4, release --features parallel, idle, best of 7, two independent runs.

This is the FOURTH kernel family measured and it moves in the OPPOSITE direction to the field kernels: 256, i.e. 16x BELOW the CPU_MULTI_MIN_WORK_ITEMS placeholder of 4096, because root finding is compute-dense per lane where field algebra is memory-bound.

Iterative solve, wall clock per whole batch (cheap residual | costly residual):

  problems   serial      multi       speedup      serial      multi       speedup
  64         12.99 us    45.16 us    0.29x        42.85 us    62.99 us    0.68x
  128        25.96 us    57.24 us    0.45x        84.88 us    86.65 us    0.98x
  256        52.94 us    42.79 us    1.24x        175.37 us   126.70 us   1.38x   <-- crossover
  1024       201.83 us   127.52 us   1.58x        695.26 us   284.70 us   2.44x
  65536      13730.89 us 5071.05 us  2.71x        45778.24 us 16260.96 us 2.82x

ROOT_BATCH_MIN_PROBLEMS = 256, the smallest size at which neither closure lost in either run. Closed-form cubics cross at 1024 (POLY_ROOTS_MIN_EQUATIONS); at 256 the two paths are exactly break-even because POLY_BLOCK is 256 and rayon never splits. Per-lane costs are comparable (~153 ns/cubic vs ~209 ns/cheap iterative lane), so the 4x gap between those two constants is a conservative reading of a noisy shallow break-even, NOT a structural claim.

RUNNING TALLY for this bead: 256 (root finding) / 4096 (LDU SpMV) / 131072 (field algebra) / 262144 (LDU vecops). A 1024x spread, with the crate-wide placeholder sitting in the middle and wrong at both ends.

AND A HARDER PROBLEM FOR THIS BEAD: the iterative root-finding crossover depends on the CALLER'S RESIDUAL COST, which the crate cannot know -- the cheap and costly closures above differ by roughly 3.3x in serial time with identical kernel code. So 'measure the crossover per kernel' is not sufficient for this family; the constant is a default, and a caller with an expensive residual should override it. Worth deciding, for this bead, whether the API should let a caller supply a measured threshold rather than inheriting a constant.

PARITY (this bead's Serial-vs-CpuMulti criterion): BITWISE IDENTICAL at 1/2/4/8 rayon workers on a deliberately imbalanced 2048-lane batch, for Brent, bisection, Newton and the cubic kernel -- every observable field (iterate, residual, bracket width, iteration count, status) compared via to_bits(). This is easier here than for ldu_matrix because a root batch has no cross-lane arithmetic and therefore no association to perturb. One documented caveat the module cannot defend against: a caller closure that is not a pure function of (i, x) breaks it.

Thread scaling, 65536 imbalanced lanes: serial 19322.52 us; 1 worker 0.94x, 2 workers 1.91x, 4 workers 2.73x (3.66x on the repeat), 8 workers 2.64x (3.57x). No gain past core count -- the compute-bound signature, in contrast to the superlinear >3x seen on 4 cores for SpMV.

ANALYTIC-ORACLE V&V: cubic roots 1/2/3 recovered EXACTLY (0.000000e0 error) by bisection, Brent and Newton. Worst |x - sqrt(k)| over 64 lanes: 1.776357e-15 (Brent), 8.881784e-16 (Newton). Mean iterations 7.73 Newton vs 13.14 Brent. Cubic batch worst residual 3.979039e-13 over 12288 real roots, worst root displacement 2.079981e-10 (near-coincident random root triples -- ill-conditioning, documented). Quadratic worst residual 7.105427e-15.

Serial-vs-Gpu parity remains ENTIRELY OPEN for this module: no GPU kernel, Gpu degrades to the best CPU path.

CAVEATS: one machine, 4 cores, idle, two runs. Not measured on Android/Termux or a many-core server. POLY_ROOTS_MIN_EQUATIONS was measured with CUBICS ONLY; quadratic and linear are cheaper per lane so they cross over later and inherit the floor as an assumption. POLY_BLOCK=256 is a granularity floor that was not swept, only verified not to change a value.

note.content:
END-TO-END SOLVER SPEED-UP, MEASURED at last — 2026-08-13. This is the first evidence in epic op-yvj.4 that any of it makes a REAL SOLVE faster; everything before this was micro-benchmarks. Fifth independent run, available_parallelism()=4, /proc/loadavg 1.53 0.85 0.37 rising to 1.67 1.00 0.45, best of 5. Asymmetric 7-point stencil.

  cells     Jacobi ser->par (ms)    speedup    ILU(0) ser->par (ms)    speedup
  4096      12.675 -> 18.785        0.67x LOSS  6.658 -> 11.075        0.60x LOSS
  32768     104.810 -> 61.699       1.70x       54.984 -> 42.558       1.29x
  512000    2024.812 -> 815.677     2.48x       1013.883 -> 676.072    1.50x

*** THE KERNEL'S CROSSOVER IS NOT THE SOLVER'S CROSSOVER. *** At 4096 cells -- EXACTLY SPMV_MIN_CELLS, the constant this bead recorded as SpMV's measured break-even -- the full solve LOSES, in all five runs. The solve only starts winning around 13000 cells. A kernel threshold measured in isolation does not transfer to the consumer that calls it, because the consumer also pays for the vector operations, the preconditioner and the residual bookkeeping, each with its own scaling. This is the most actionable thing on this bead: per-kernel constants are necessary but NOT sufficient, and a caller needs its own crossover.

ILU(0) IS THE BRAKE, quantified rather than asserted. Both phases have loop-carried dependence and are not parallelised. Triangular solves are 29-46% of serial solve time (four runs: 34.1 / 37.4 / 37.3 / 40.7%), which by Amdahl caps attainable speed-up at 1.7-2.1x on 4 cores. Measured 1.50x sits BELOW that cap, so ILU(0) dominates but is not the only limit. Factorisation costs a further 23.8% of one serial solve per coefficient update.

REDUCTION-ORDER SAFETY, now measured instead of argued. The concern recorded earlier on this bead was that ldu_matrix::parallel's blocked dot is not bit-equal to krylov::vecops' flat sum (worst 2.3744e-13) and could flip an iteration count near a convergence tolerance. Swept 216 solve pairs -- 3 sizes x 3 dominances x 3 seeds x 4 tolerances (1e-6 to 1e-12) x 2 solvers: ZERO iteration-count flips. GMRES was included and had never been compared before; it is the more exposed solver, with roughly 4x the reductions per iteration and a stopping test that reads a Givens recurrence rather than a fresh norm. Max relative residual difference 2.220e-4, which sounds alarming but is an ABSOLUTE difference of ~1.9e-16 on a residual of 8.6e-13. The BiCGStab worst case stopped at 0.86x its own tolerance -- about as near the deciding boundary as the grid reaches -- and still did not flip. Zero flips in 216 pairs bounds the rate at roughly 1-in-216 for systems of this kind; it is NOT proof that no system flips.

Serial vs CpuMulti is BIT-EXACT for both solvers including every residual-history entry, not merely the final answer.

TWO SELF-CORRECTIONS the agent made from its own printed output, worth recording because they are the failure mode this epic keeps hitting: a predecessor's claim that 'GMRES gains less than BiCGStab at every size tested' is FALSE at 4096 cells, where GMRES was ahead (0.78x vs 0.67x) -- now restricted to >=32768 cells; and an uncomputed range '23.8-24.7% across four runs' had been written into preconditioner.rs and was replaced with the single figure actually paired.

CAVEATS: one virtualised 4-core host that never idles (bn daemon ~37% of a core); one matrix family; f64 CPU only. There is NO GPU kernel in this path at all, so nothing here speaks to ComputeBackend::Gpu and the Serial-vs-Gpu half of this bead remains entirely open. Absolute milliseconds are not comparable across sessions -- serial times shifted ~2x between container restarts at LOWER load -- so only ratios should be read.

note.content:
BLOCKED, and not for the reason the bead anticipated. Checked 2026-08-13 before briefing any agent on it.

The bead's own scope note says: do not build this first, land op-yvj.4.1 and at least one batched kernel plus its benchmark so there are real crossover numbers to pick a split ratio from. That precondition is now MET and then some -- op-yvj.4.1 is closed, and seven kernel families have measured crossovers (16 ODE / 32 quadrature / 256 root finding / 256 minimisation / 4096 LDU SpMV / 131072 field algebra / 262144 LDU vecops), plus an end-to-end solver measurement from op-yvj.4.4.

THE ACTUAL BLOCKER: there is NO GPU KERNEL ANYWHERE IN outram-foam-basic-lib. Verified by grep -- no  usage outside compute.rs's adapter probe, and no WGSL/@compute/@workgroup_size anywhere; the two apparent hits are doc-comment prose about WGSL lacking f64. Every landed module routes ComputeBackend::Gpu to the best available CPU path, and each says so in its docs. The cross-cutting parity gate (tests/hybrid_parity.rs) asserts exactly this: all seven dispatch-policy functions are queried for Gpu at n = 2^22 and asserted NEVER to return it.

So co-execution -- 'run CpuMulti and Gpu concurrently on one batch' -- has nothing to co-execute with. A Hybrid split policy dividing lanes between CpuMulti and a Gpu path that itself resolves to CpuMulti would be pure theatre: it would add a split ratio, a determinism caveat and a mixed-precision caveat to a computation that runs entirely on the CPU either way. Building it now would produce code that looks like an optimisation and is not one.

BOTH of the bead's own 'settle before implementing' caveats are also unreachable today for the same reason: mixed precision within one result cannot arise when no lane runs at f32, and the reproducibility question about a dynamic split reordering reductions cannot be measured against a GPU half that does not exist.

WHAT UNBLOCKS IT: a real GPU kernel for at least one embarrassingly-parallel family. op-3ep6 is the nearest candidate (GPU fixed-rule quadrature), filed by the op-yvj.4.5 agent, which noted the real difficulty is the caller-supplied Rust closure rather than the arithmetic -- a WGSL kernel cannot call an arbitrary Rust , so the batched-kernel APIs that take closures are structurally hard to move to the GPU. That is worth settling before op-3ep6 too.

SECOND-ORDER BLOCKER even once a kernel exists: this container HAS NO GPU ADAPTER. compute.rs's probe returns false here, so a GPU kernel could be written but not executed or verified. op-b4a.4.8 already tracks 'validate wgpu dispatch on a real GPU host' workspace-wide. Any GPU work landed from this environment would ship unexecuted, which is exactly what op-0nh (f32 Faddeeva accuracy) is already open about elsewhere.

RECOMMENDATION: leave this bead Todo and do not implement it speculatively. It should be picked up after a GPU kernel exists AND on a host with an adapter. Nothing else in op-yvj.4 depends on it.

note.content:
Closed as GitHub #18. src/compute/hybrid.rs, commit 2c3c1ac641.

Delivered form 2 (data-level co-execution) — the one this bead called the direct answer and easiest real speedup. SplitPlan is a selection policy over the existing CpuMulti and Gpu paths, containing no numerical code, exactly as specified — not a fourth implementation of every kernel.

Both caveats this bead required be settled BEFORE implementation are settled in the API, not in prose:
- Mixed precision: SplitPlan::precision_note() states per call that leading lanes are f64 and trailing lanes f32 and accuracy is not uniform; CoExecution::MatchGpuPrecision offers uniform f32-grade accuracy for callers who would rather lose good bits than have a seam. Default is NativePrecision — silently degrading correct arithmetic is the worse default.
- Reproducibility: the split is static and deterministic, a pure function of lane count and ratio, no timing/sampling/RNG. Dynamic work-stealing is NOT offered at all rather than offered unused, because the moment it exists someone gets a non-reproducible reduction without reading why.

SplitRatio::Measured resolves to ZERO GPU lanes — that is the measurement, not a placeholder (see op-yvj.4.7). A planner that truthfully says 'do not use the GPU here' is doing its job.

Forms 1 (task-level concurrency) and 3 (transfer/compute overlap) deliberately not implemented: both need genuinely async dispatch, and GpuContext::dispatch currently blocks on readback. Recorded in the module's 'Not implemented, deliberately' section.

Ordering honoured: this bead said not to build before real crossover numbers existed. They exist now, which is what makes the default ratio a measurement instead of a guess.

note.content:
Implemented. crates/kovan/src/digitiser/gui/desktop/pdf_reader.rs:
- New "Select text" tool alongside "Select"/"Draw box", using `kopitiam_pdf::mupdf::page_to_stext` (MuPDF's structured-text model, real per-line device-space bboxes -- not OCR, not pixel-region annotation).
- New free function `select_text_in_rect(page, scale, min, max) -> String`: concatenates the text of every StextLine whose bbox (converted from PDF points to this panel's texture-pixel space by `RENDER_DPI/72.0`, the same scale `rasterize_page` itself applies) intersects the drag rect. Line granularity, not character/glyph granularity -- documented as a deliberate scope cut in the module doc.
- `stext_for_page` caches the current page's `StextPage` (re-extracted on page change only, not kept for every page -- a full-res StextPage is a lot more data per page than a thumbnail texture).
- `text_selection_panel`: shows the last selection with Copy-to-clipboard and "Save as annotation" (folds the selection into the same `annotations` markdown section op-96am's hand-typed notes use).
- 4 new unit tests for `select_text_in_rect` against a hand-built `StextPage` fixture (intersection filtering, the DPI-scale conversion specifically, multi-line join, no-intersection case) -- exercises the real kopitiam_pdf types, not a mock.

Known limitation, disclosed rather than silently assumed away: the device-space-to-pixel-space conversion assumes the page has no rotation quirk beyond what `page_to_stext`'s own `page_mediabox` already handles internally -- not independently verified against `rasterize_page`'s own `page_is_quarter_turned` swap for a rotated page, since no rotated-page test fixture was available in this pass. Flagging this explicitly rather than claiming full verification; worth a real-PDF smoke test with a rotated page if that turns out to matter in practice.

cargo check --all-targets clean (native + aarch64-linux-android). cargo test --release: 191 kovan lib tests passing (8 new in pdf_reader alone this round). cargo doc --no-deps: no new warnings. Not committed yet.
